proved_step: statement: AFFINE RESIDUAL STATE BOUND. Let A be an r×N matrix over GF(2), c∈GF(2)^r, and F={x∈{0,1}^N: Ax=c}. At a cut t, write A=(A_<t | D_+), where A_<t consists of the first t columns and D_+ the remaining columns. For prefix p∈{0,1}^t, its exact residual is R_t(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}:D_+z=c+A_<t p}. The number of distinct residuals over all p is at most 2^r. They admit an exact r-bit state y(p)=c+A_<t p, with next-bit update y(pb)=y(p)+b a_t, where a_t is column t of A; the update uses O(r) fan-in-two Boolean gates. Proof: The displayed residual identity follows by splitting Ax=c into prefix and suffix terms; subtraction equals addition over GF(2). Each prefix maps to one of at most 2^r vectors y∈GF(2)^r, and y determines its residual set by the displayed equation, so there are at most 2^r residuals. Appending b changes the prefix contribution by b a_t, proving the update formula. Each output coordinate is either the corresponding input bit or its XOR with the fixed bit (a_t)_i when b=1; implementing the r conditional XORs costs O(r) fan-in-two gates. This is an exact bound for the affine language subclass only; it gives no transition bound for arbitrary EXT or MCSP decision circuits.

statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL UPDATE BOUND. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and 0≤t<N. Let D_t be the set of distinct residuals R_t(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pz∈F} over prefixes p∈{0,1}^t, and d_t=|D_t|. Encode a current residual R∈D_t by its one-hot indicator vector indexed by D_t. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit, depending only on F and t, that on this vector and next input bit b outputs the one-hot encoding of R_b={u∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}:bu∈R}; its size is at most 6d_t+1. Proof: For every R∈D_t and b∈{0,1}, form token q_{R,b}=x_R∧ℓ_b, where ℓ_1=b and ℓ_0=¬b. This uses 2d_t AND gates and at most one NOT gate. For each R'∈D_{t+1}, output y_{R'} as the OR of all tokens q_{R,b} whose section R_b equals R'; if there are none, output constant 0. Each pair (R,b) has exactly one section in D_{t+1}, since R is itself a residual R_t(p), and R_b=R_{t+1}(pb). Hence the token groups partition the 2d_t tokens. Binary OR trees use at most 2d_t additional gates in total. For a one-hot input x_R*, exactly the token for R* and the actual b is 1, so exactly its successor output is 1 and all others are 0. Total size is at most 4d_t+1, hence at most 6d_t+1. This is a bound for the canonical one-hot residual representation only; it proves neither a polynomial bound on d_t for EXT_{n,s} nor a transition bound from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

statement: FIXED-ORACLE STREAMING STATES BOUND RESIDUALS. Let F be a language of fixed-length strings {0,1}^N. Suppose a deterministic streaming decider M reads input left to right, has at most 2^w internal configurations at every cut (including all persistent work-tape contents and control state), and may make queries to one fixed oracle O. For each cut t, the number d_t of distinct residuals R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} is at most 2^w. Proof: Associate to each length-t prefix p the complete configuration c(p) reached after reading p. If c(p)=c(q), then for every suffix z, the future computation on z from that configuration is identical for pz and qz: the machine is deterministic, and every oracle query receives the same answer from the same fixed O. Hence pz is accepted iff qz is accepted for every z, so R_t(p)=R_t(q). Thus the map from reachable configurations at cut t onto residuals is well-defined and surjective, giving d_t≤|configurations|≤2^w. Scope: this is an exact state-count implication for deterministic fixed-oracle streaming deciders. It does not bound the cost of an oracle transition, does not imply a polynomial-size ordinary circuit for EXT or MCSP, and does not transfer a streaming state lower bound to general circuits.

statement: TIME-VARYING TRANSITION UNROLLING. Let M be a deterministic machine reading inputs x_1,...,x_N in order, with a w-bit state after each step. Suppose for each i its state update from (state,x_i) to the next state is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most T gates, and its final accept/reject output from the last state is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most T gates. Then M's decision function on {0,1}^N has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most NT+T gates. Proof: Construct a layered circuit with one copy of the i-th update circuit at each position i, wiring its state inputs to the preceding layer and its input-bit input to x_i; initialize the first layer with M's fixed initial-state constants. By induction on i, the wires after layer i equal M's state after reading x_1,...,x_i. Apply the final decision circuit to the last layer. The resulting circuit computes M's decision function, and its gate count is at most the sum of N update-circuit sizes plus T, hence at most NT+T. Scope: this is conditional on ordinary fan-in-two circuits for every transition. It does not simulate oracle transitions or establish such circuits for the MMW19 EXT prefix machine.

statement: CANDIDATE-FILTERING AUTOMATON FOR EXT. Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be any finite indexed family of words in {0,1}^N, allowing duplicates, and let L_F={f_i:i<=M}. At depth t and prefix p in {0,1}^t, store q_p in {0,1}^M with q_p[i]=1 iff f_i has prefix p. The residual of L_F after p is exactly {f_i[t:N]:q_p[i]=1}. On reading b, update q_p to q_pb by q_pb[i]=q_p[i] AND [f_i(t)=b]. Thus the update is a stage-specific fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most M AND gates (the selectors [f_i(t)=b] are constants), and EXT acceptance at a prefix is the OR of the M state bits. Proof: For each i, f_i has prefix pb iff it has prefix p and its t-th coordinate equals b, proving the update coordinatewise. A suffix z is in the residual iff some i with q_p[i]=1 has suffix f_i[t:N]=z, precisely the definition of membership in L_F after prefix p. The disjunction of state bits is true iff at least one listed word extends p. For EXT_{n,s}, take F to be the indexed list of truth tables of all size-at-most-s circuits; this gives an exact, generally exponential-state representation and an O(M)-gate update after stage-specific candidate bits are available. It does not bound transition cost by a bounded number of operations on H_C or imply a statement about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Maintain one live bit per candidate truth table. Inductively q_p[i]=1 iff candidate i matches the consumed prefix. After b, candidate i remains live exactly when q_p[i]=1 and its fixed t-th output equals b. This establishes the update, residual characterization, and acceptance test.

For each prefix p in {0,1}^t, 0<=t<=N, define q_p in {0,1}^M by q_p[i]=1 iff f_i[1..t]=p. Then p is an extendable prefix of F (that is, there exists f in F with prefix p) if and only if OR_i q_p[i]=1. For t<N and b in {0,1}, q_{pb}[i]=q_p[i] AND [f_i[t+1]=b]. Given the stage-t candidate-output bits a_i=[f_i[t+1]=b], this transition and acceptance test have Boolean circuits of O(M) fan-in-2 gates. Proof: By definition, q_p[i]=1 exactly for indices whose word agrees with p on the first t positions. Such a word exists precisely when at least one coordinate is 1, proving the acceptance equivalence. An index agrees with pb exactly when it agrees with p and its next bit equals b, which is the displayed coordinatewise conjunction. Implement M conjunction gates and an OR tree with M-1 gates (with the M=1 boundary handled by a wire); total O(M). The argument gives a uniform construction from the explicit family and stage bits, but makes no claim that those bits or the family can be constructed in polynomial time from an arbitrary circuit class H_C.

statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY FOR EXACT STREAMING STATES. Let F be a language of binary strings of length N and fix 0<=t<=N. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}, and let d_t be the number of distinct such residual sets. Any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that decides F exactly after reading all N bits must have at least d_t distinct internal states after t input bits. Proof: If prefixes p and q lead to the same internal state, then determinism implies that for every common suffix z the algorithm has the same final state and output on pz and qz. Exactness therefore implies pz in F iff qz in F for every z, so R_t(p)=R_t(q). Thus prefixes inducing distinct residuals must induce distinct internal states, giving at least d_t states. Consequently the workspace is at least ceil(log2 d_t) bits. This is a representation-independent workspace bound; it gives no lower bound on update time and does not establish that d_t is large for EXT_{n,s}.

statement: TRACE-COFACTOR UNIQUENESS LEMMA. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with g gates, input x in {0,1}^N, and designated output gate o. Introduce one witness bit y_i per gate and define H_C(x,y) as the conjunction of y_o=1 and, for each gate i, y_i equals gate_i(x,y_{<i}), with gates in topological order. Then (i) for every x there is exactly one y satisfying all gate equations, namely C's evaluation trace; (ii) H_C(x,y)=1 exactly when C(x)=1 and y is that trace; (iii) fixing any input prefix p gives H_{C,p}(z,y)=H_C(pz,y), with the same gate equations and a unique trace for every z. Thus exists y H_{C,p}(z,y)=C(pz).
derivation: Induct in topological gate order. Given x and the earlier witness bits, gate i has a uniquely determined Boolean value, so its equation forces exactly one y_i. This proves existence and uniqueness of the complete trace. The output conjunct holds exactly when the trace's output bit is 1, proving (ii). For (iii), substitute the fixed prefix constants into the input wires. This changes no gate equation and adds no witness choices, so the same induction gives one trace for each suffix z. Existentially quantifying that trace accepts exactly when C(pz)=1. This establishes exact cofactoring of the verifier relation; it does not bound the cost of compiling its existential projection from H_C alone.
scope: Finite fan-in-two Boolean circuits with a fixed topological gate order, any input length, and any fixed prefix. No bound is claimed for compiling the projection z -> exists y H_{C,p}(z,y) from a succinct H_C description, nor for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: REPAIRED LAYERED RESIDUAL IMPLEMENTATION BOUND. For any L subset {0,1}^N, let r_t be the number of distinct residual languages after length-t prefixes. A deterministic length-N recognizer with position-dependent transitions uses max_t r_t state labels, and at least r_t labels are necessary at each fixed depth t.
derivation: Set W=max_t r_t. For each t, inject the residuals at depth t into [W] using a code c_t. Initialize at c_0(L). At layer t, on bit b, send c_t(R) to c_{t+1}(R_b), where R_b={z:bz in R}. This is well-defined because the source code identifies R and R_b is determined by R. Define transitions arbitrarily on labels unused at layer t. At depth N accept c_N(R) exactly when the empty string belongs to R. By induction the state after prefix p is c_t(R_t(p)), so the machine recognizes L. Reuse across layers is valid because the transition function may depend on t and acceptance is terminal. Conversely, two distinct residuals at the same depth cannot share a state: a suffix distinguishing them would then have to produce the same acceptance. Hence at least r_t labels are necessary at depth t.
scope: Finite Boolean language of fixed length N; deterministic recognizer with position-dependent transitions and terminal acceptance. This bounds state labels only and says nothing about gate cost for succinctly implementing transitions.

statement: BOUNDED-SUFFIX PROJECTION LEMMA. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with g gates, input x=(u,z) where z has k bits, and output C(u,z). Define P(u)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^k with C(u,z)=1. Then P has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^k g + 2^k - 1: take one copy of C(u,z) for each fixed assignment a to z, substitute z=a, and OR the 2^k outputs in a binary tree. In particular, for fixed k this is O(g) and the construction is uniform given C and k.
derivation: For each a in {0,1}^k, let C_a(u)=C(u,a), formed by substituting constants on the z-input wires. Substitution preserves correctness and uses at most g gates. The circuit P'(u)=OR_{a in {0,1}^k} C_a(u) accepts exactly when at least one suffix assignment makes C(u,z)=1, which is precisely the definition of P. A binary OR tree combines 2^k outputs using 2^k-1 fan-in-two gates. Thus the total is at most 2^k g+2^k-1. The construction does not provide polynomial size when k grows as an unrestricted input parameter, and it says nothing about eliminating an existential trace of an arbitrary succinct relation unless the relation is represented by the circuit C itself.
scope: Boolean circuits with a designated set of k existentially quantified input bits; fixed k gives linear-size projection. No general polynomial bound in g and k, no lower bound, and no conclusion for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits when k is large.
diagnostic_barriers: Relativizing: the enumeration identity relativizes for ordinary Boolean cofactoring. Natural: no lower bound claimed. Algebrizing: no algebraic argument claimed. Localizing: no lower bound claimed. Circumvention tests inapplicable: this is a restricted algorithmic lemma, not P!=NP progress.

statement: FIXED-VERIFIER COFACTOR COST LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For any fixed prefix p∈{0,1}^t, the relation H_p(z,w)=H(pz,w), on z∈{0,1}^{N−t} and w∈{0,1}^r, is computable by a fan-in-two circuit with at most h gates. Its existential projection L_p(z)=1 iff ∃w H_p(z,w)=1 is exactly the residual of L(x)=1 iff ∃w H(x,w)=1 after prefix p. For b∈{0,1}, H_{pb} is obtained by further fixing one input bit and still uses at most h gates. This gives no circuit-size bound for L_p itself and no update bound for maintaining all size-s circuit candidates.
derivation: Keep the original circuit graph and replace each input wire corresponding to a fixed prefix coordinate by its fixed Boolean constant; leave all other input wires unchanged. Each gate and edge is retained, so the gate count is at most h. For every suffix z and witness w, the resulting circuit evaluates to H(pz,w) by substitution, hence ∃w H_p(z,w)=1 iff ∃w H(pz,w)=1, which is precisely membership in the residual after p. Fixing the next input bit b is the same substitution on one more input wire, so again does not add gates. Existential projection is only an equality of relations here; the construction has not eliminated w or produced a Boolean circuit for the projected language.
scope: All finite Boolean relations represented by fan-in-two circuits; exact cofactoring of fixed input coordinates only. Diagnostic labels: relativizing—yes, the substitution identity remains valid relative to any fixed oracle gate model if oracle wires are untouched; natural—no lower-bound method is asserted; algebrizing—no algebraic extension is asserted; localizing—no lower bound is asserted. Circumvention checks: reversible computing, Strassen cancellation, Barrington width-5, catalytic space, and mass production are inapplicable to this circuit-substitution identity.

statement: BOUNDED-SUFFIX EXTENSION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, and fix a prefix p of length N−k. The predicate E_p(u)=1 iff there exists v∈{0,1}^k with H(puv)=1, for u∈{0,1}^0 (or, more generally, with p fixed and the k remaining input bits free), has a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^k(h+k+1) gates. In particular, for k≤c log₂(h+2), it has polynomial size in h for each fixed constant c. This bounds explicit suffix elimination for one fixed circuit; it does not represent the existential set of all size-s candidate circuits.
derivation: For each v∈{0,1}^k, cofactor H by fixing the k suffix inputs to v. Input substitution leaves at most h gates and computes the corresponding restricted predicate. Take the OR of these 2^k predicates using a binary OR tree with at most 2^k−1 additional gates. If u denotes any other unfixed input coordinates, preserve them in each cofactor. The resulting circuit accepts exactly when at least one suffix v makes H accept, by the definition of OR. The total is at most 2^k h+(2^k−1), which is at most 2^k(h+k+1). For k≤c log₂(h+2), 2^k≤(h+2)^c, so the bound is polynomial in h for fixed c. The construction enumerates suffixes of one fixed H; it does not enumerate or update the family of candidate circuits defining EXT.
scope: Fan-in-two Boolean circuits, fixed H and explicitly bounded suffix length k. This is a constructive circuit upper bound, not a lower bound or P!=NP progress. Diagnostic labels: relativizing—yes, cofactoring and OR composition remain valid with fixed oracle gates; natural—no lower-bound argument; algebrizing—no algebraic extension; localizing—no lower-bound argument. Circumvention tests (reversible computing, Strassen cancellation, Barrington width five, catalytic space, mass production) are not invoked; the construction makes no unavoidable-cost claim.

statement: BOUNDED-WITNESS PROJECTION LEMMA. For every fan-in-two Boolean circuit C(u,z) with g gates and z in {0,1}^k, P(u)=1 iff there exists z C(u,z)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^k g + 2^k - 1 gates. Proof: for each assignment a in {0,1}^k, substitute a into C, obtaining C_a(u) with at most g gates. Combine the 2^k outputs with a binary OR tree using 2^k-1 gates. Their OR is true exactly when some witness satisfies C. Therefore the total gate count is at most 2^k g+2^k-1. In particular, for fixed k the cost is O(g); for growing k this bound may be exponential in k. This establishes a bounded-witness projection case only, not a polynomial transition bound for unrestricted EXT.
derivation: Enumerate all witness assignments, substitute constants into C, and OR the resulting circuit outputs.
scope: Fan-in-two Boolean circuits; k existential Boolean witness inputs; arbitrary remaining input u; gate count only.
barriers: Diagnostic: relativizing identity; no natural, algebrizing, or localizing lower-bound method asserted; circumvention tests inapplicable because no P!=NP claim is made.

statement: EXPLICIT LAYERED TRANSITION CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let Q be a nonempty state set of size m, S=ceil(log2 m), and for each of N input positions let δ_i:Q×{0,1}→Q be an arbitrary transition map. Fix an injective encoding e:Q→{0,1}^S. Each encoded next-state map (q,b)↦e(δ_i(q,b)) has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most S(S+2)2^(S+1) gates; thus all N transitions have at most N S(S+2)2^(S+1) gates. The construction is effective from the explicit transition tables. For m=1, zero state bits suffice and every transition is constant, so the bound is zero. This bounds implementation cost given a table, not the cost of obtaining the table from H_C.
derivation: For m≥2, S≥1. For each output coordinate j, view its value as a Boolean function f_j of d=S+1 input bits (the S state bits and the input bit). Its truth-table DNF has at most 2^d minterms. Each minterm is an AND of d literals and can be built with at most d−1 fan-in-two AND gates; literals are input bits or their negations, with at most d NOT gates shared across all output coordinates. The OR of at most 2^d minterms uses at most 2^d−1 fan-in-two OR gates. A safe per-coordinate bound including separately charged literal negations is d·2^d + (2^d−1); multiplying by S is at most S(d+1)2^d = S(S+2)2^(S+1). Empty DNFs implement constant zero. Applying this independently for each i yields the total. The construction reads the table entries to form each truth table, so it is effective with O(Nm) table lookups, but assumes δ_i is explicitly supplied.
scope: Finite deterministic layered automata with arbitrary position-dependent binary transitions and explicit transition tables; arbitrary injective state encoding of length ceil(log2 m). Does not bound the cost of constructing transition tables from a succinct MCSP decision circuit H_C, so the original EXT-to-H_C gap remains open. Diagnostic labels: relativizing—yes, the finite truth-table construction is unchanged relative to a fixed oracle model when transitions are explicit; natural—no lower-bound method; algebrizing—no algebraic extension; localizing—no lower-bound method. Circumvention tests: reversible computing, Strassen cancellation, Barrington width five, catalytic space, and mass production are not invoked; no P!=NP claim.

statement: WITNESS-ENUMERATION PROJECTION BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For any fixed prefix p of x of length t, the residual R_p(z)=1 iff ∃w∈{0,1}^r H(pz,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r h + (2^r−1) gates. Proof: For each w∈{0,1}^r, substitute p and w into H, obtaining a circuit H_{p,w}(z) with at most h gates. Form their disjunction over all 2^r assignments w using a binary OR tree with 2^r−1 gates. At each z, this OR is 1 exactly when at least one witness w satisfies H(pz,w), which is the definition of R_p. Substitution cannot increase gate count. For r=0 the construction is just H_p and uses at most h gates. This is an exact upper bound, not a lower bound; it makes explicit that direct witness elimination costs exponential in witness length and therefore does not establish a polynomial-gate transition from H_C without additional structure.
derivation: Circuit input substitution for each fixed witness retains at most h gates. Enumerate the finite witness set (2^r assignments), build one copy per assignment, and combine the outputs by a binary OR tree. Correctness follows pointwise from the existential quantifier. Total gates ≤2^r h+2^r−1; the empty-witness-bit case is included.
scope: All finite Boolean relations represented by fan-in-two circuits; arbitrary fixed prefix p; witness length r. Diagnostic: this constructive upper bound is relativizing in form; it claims no lower bound or P≠NP progress, so natural/algebrizing/localizing status and circumvention tests are not invoked.

statement: LOGARITHMIC-WITNESS PROJECTION COROLLARY. Let H(x,w) have h>=1 fan-in-two gates and r witness bits. If r<=c log2(h) for a fixed c>=0, then every fixed-prefix existential residual R_p(z)=exists w H(pz,w) has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most h^(c+1)+h^c.
derivation: By S0798's witness-enumeration construction, the size is at most 2^r h+2^r-1. Since r<=c log2 h, 2^r<=h^c. Therefore the size is at most h^(c+1)+h^c. This is polynomial in h for fixed c and applies to every prefix.
scope: All finite fan-in-two Boolean circuits with h>=1 and witness length r<=c log2 h; fixed c. It gives polynomial projection cost only under this witness-length restriction.
diagnostic: This is an upper-bound construction, not a lower bound or P!=NP progress. It is relativizing in form; the other barrier labels and circumvention tests are not asserted.

statement: SELF-CONTAINED LOGARITHMIC-WITNESS PROJECTION LEMMA. Let H(x,w) be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h>=1 gates, and let w have r bits. For any fixed prefix p of x, if r<=c log2(h) for fixed c>=0, the residual R_p(z)=1 iff there exists w H(pz,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most h^(c+1)+h^c.
derivation: For each of the 2^r assignments a to w, substitute p and a into H, producing a circuit on z with at most h gates. Combine these 2^r outputs with a binary OR tree using 2^r-1 gates. Pointwise, the result is 1 exactly when some assignment a satisfies H(pz,a), so it computes R_p. Its size is at most 2^r h+2^r-1. Since r<=c log2(h), 2^r<=h^c, and hence the size is at most h^(c+1)+h^c. This proof constructs the circuit directly and uses no earlier claimed step.
scope: All finite fan-in-two Boolean circuits with h>=1, fixed c>=0, witness length r<=c log2(h), and arbitrary fixed prefixes p. This is a polynomial upper bound only in the stated logarithmic-witness regime; it gives no lower bound or general MCSP transition bound.
diagnostic: This is an upper-bound construction, not a P!=NP claim. No barrier circumvention claim is made.

statement: FINITE-LIST RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let A be a listed multiset of M strings in {0,1}^N. At every depth t, the number r_t of distinct residual sets induced by prefixes of length t is at most min(2^t,M+1). Consequently sum_{t=0}^N r_t <= (N+1)(M+1). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so r_t<=2^t. For each prefix p let I_p be the list indices whose strings extend p. Distinct length-t prefixes have disjoint index sets, so there are at most M nonempty sets I_p, plus at most one empty set. Hence r_t<=M+1. Summing gives the consequence.
derivation: For every depth t, map each prefix p to I_p={j: a_j begins with p}. Distinct prefixes induce disjoint index sets. Therefore at most M distinct nonempty residual index sets occur, and at most one empty set; also there are at most 2^t prefixes. These yield r_t<=min(2^t,M+1), and summing the M+1 bound across N+1 depths proves the total bound.
scope: All finite N,t and explicit listed multisets A, including M=0. This bounds state counts for the listed language only and does not bound transition-gate costs from a succinct description H_C.
diagnostic: Upper bound only; no lower-bound or P!=NP claim.

statement: RESIDUAL-TABLE TRANSITION CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let L be a subset of {0,1}^N. At depth t, let r_t be the number of distinct residual languages and encode them by indices 0,...,r_t-1. If the explicit transition table mapping each state index and next input bit to the next residual index is supplied, then for r_t>=1 the transition map at that layer has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size O(r_t log(r_{t+1})), with state input width ceil(log2 r_t) and output width ceil(log2 r_{t+1}). The table is well-defined because a residual language determines both of its sections. Proof: For each current index i, construct an equality indicator e_i for the binary state input using O(log r_t) fan-in-two gates. For each output bit k, OR together e_i over exactly those indices whose transition on the given input bit has output bit k equal to 1, using O(r_t) gates per output bit; do this for both input-bit values, selected by the input bit. This costs O(r_t log r_t + r_t log r_{t+1}) gates, hence O(r_t(log r_t+log r_{t+1})); since r_{t+1}<=2r_t for residuals, this is O(r_t log r_{t+1}) when r_{t+1}>=2, and the constant-width boundary cases take O(r_t) gates. The construction compiles a supplied table and does not bound the cost of generating it from a succinct description.
derivation: Equality decoding plus per-output-bit OR of the table entries, separately for each of the two input bits; residual sections ensure table consistency.
scope: Deterministic layered recognizer for a finite Boolean language; transition table supplied explicitly; fan-in-two Boolean circuits. This gives a real-gate implementation bound but no succinct-table generation bound and no arbitrary MCSP decision-circuit lower bound.
diagnostic_barriers: This is an upper-bound construction only; it makes no P!=NP progress claim and asserts no barrier circumvention.

refuted_approach: S0802 as stated claims O(r_t log r_{t+1}) from an equality-decoding construction, but its proof also incurs O(r_t log r_t) gates. The claimed simplification is invalid when r_{t+1} is small (notably r_{t+1}=1 while r_t>1); the bound must retain the state-decoding term.
evidence: Direct gate count in the S0802 construction: decoding r_t possible state indices requires O(r_t ceil(log2 r_t)) equality-test gates. The output OR networks require O(r_t ceil(log2 r_{t+1})) gates per input-bit branch, plus selection. The asserted asymptotic absorption does not follow when r_{t+1} is small.

statement: REPAIRED RESIDUAL-TABLE TRANSITION CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let L subset {0,1}^N and r_i be the number of distinct residual languages at depth i. Suppose the transition table from depth t residual indices and the next input bit to depth t+1 residual indices is explicitly supplied, with canonical binary indices. For r_t,r_{t+1}>=1, each position-specific transition map has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size O(r_t ceil(log2 r_t)+r_t ceil(log2 r_{t+1})+ceil(log2 r_{t+1})). Proof: For each legal current index i, build its equality indicator by comparing the ceil(log2 r_t) state bits against the fixed binary code of i, using O(ceil(log2 r_t)) fan-in-two gates; this costs O(r_t ceil(log2 r_t)). For each of the two values b of the next input bit and each output bit k, OR the equality indicators for those i whose table entry on b has output bit k equal to 1. The OR costs O(r_t) per (b,k), so all such ORs cost O(r_t ceil(log2 r_{t+1})). Select between the two branch outputs using b, costing O(ceil(log2 r_{t+1})). For every legal state code and each b, exactly one equality indicator is true, so the selected output equals the supplied table entry. Invalid state codes may map arbitrarily. Residual sections make the table semantically well-defined. The empty-language boundary can instead use a single rejecting state and constant transitions.
derivation: One-hot equality decoding for each legal state index followed by per-output-bit ORs for each input-bit branch and a final bit-controlled selection. Retaining both logarithmic factors avoids the invalid absorption in S0802 when r_{t+1} is small.
scope: Finite fixed-length Boolean language; explicitly supplied position-specific residual transition table; canonical binary state codes; fan-in-two Boolean circuits. No bound on generating the table from a succinct circuit description, and no lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
diagnostic_barriers: Upper-bound construction only; makes no P!=NP progress claim. The finite workflow verification cm-d06efb0dd36149ce checked related table arithmetic on 4,355 small cases, but is not proof of this general circuit-size bound.

statement: EXPLICIT WITNESS-ELIMINATION BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, with constants and fixed input substitutions free. For any fixed prefix p, the projected residual E_p(z)=1 iff there exists w∈{0,1}^r with H(pz,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^r h + 2^r − 1 gates. Proof: For each of the 2^r witness strings w, substitute p and w into H, obtaining a circuit on z with at most h gates computing H(pz,w). Take the OR of these 2^r outputs using a binary tree with 2^r−1 OR gates. The resulting circuit outputs 1 exactly when at least one witness makes H(pz,w)=1, which is E_p(z). This also covers r=0, where there is one cofactor and zero OR gates. The bound is exact as a construction upper bound; it does not assert that projection requires this many gates, nor provide a polynomial bound when r grows.
derivation: Enumerate all witness strings, cofactor H at each string and the fixed prefix, then OR the resulting outputs. Each cofactor preserves the h-gate bound; a binary OR of q outputs uses q−1 gates. Set q=2^r.
scope: Finite Boolean relation, fan-in-two circuit, free constants and input substitution; fixed prefix and r witness bits.

Then for every suffix z of length N−t−1, R_{pb}(z)=R_p(bz). Proof: R_{pb}(z)=1 iff ∃w H(pbz,w)=1. By concatenation pbz=p(bz), this is equivalent to ∃w H(p(bz),w)=1, which is R_p(bz)=1. The identity preserves the existential witness domain exactly; it does not construct a circuit for the projected residual or bound the cost of evaluating it.

statement: EXPLICIT WITNESS ENUMERATION FOR PROJECTED RESIDUALS. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be given by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. Define L(x)=1 iff ∃w H(x,w)=1. For a prefix p of length t, define R_p(z)=1 iff ∃w H(pz,w)=1. Given p,z, R_p(z) can be evaluated exactly in at most 2^r circuit evaluations, hence at most 2^r h gate evaluations, using O(h+N+r) working bits in addition to the read-only circuit description. For b∈{0,1}, R_{pb}(z')=R_p(bz'). Proof: enumerate the 2^r witnesses w and accept iff one circuit evaluation H(pz,w) is 1; this is equivalent by the definition of existential quantification. The working storage can hold one circuit evaluation's gate values and the input/witness counters, within O(h+N+r) bits. Finally, R_{pb}(z')=1 iff ∃w H(pb z',w)=1 iff ∃w H(p(bz'),w)=1 iff R_p(bz'). This gives an exact projected-residual evaluator and transition identity; its 2^r factor does not establish an efficient transition for succinct EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: For fixed p,z, existential truth is equivalent to at least one of the finitely many 2^r assignments making H(pz,w)=1. Evaluating the h-gate circuit separately on each assignment gives the stated time; storing gate values for one evaluation and counters gives the workspace bound. The transition identity follows by associativity of concatenation and the unchanged witness domain.
scope: All finite N,r,h and all Boolean circuits H of the stated type.

statement: CORRECTED LAYERED RESIDUAL STATE COUNT. For L subset {0,1}^N, let r_t count distinct residual languages at depth t. With position-dependent transitions and a shared state set, the minimum number of states is max_t r_t. If layer labels must be disjoint, the minimum number of layer-state copies is sum_t r_t.
derivation: At depth t, prefixes with different residuals need different states: some suffix distinguishes them. Thus at least max_t r_t states are necessary. Let R=max_t r_t and assign each layer's residuals distinct codes from a common palette of R states. At position t, send the code for residual A on bit b to the code for A_b={z:bz in A}. This is well-defined because A determines both sections. Induction shows the state encodes the current residual, so acceptance is exact. With disjoint layer copies, the per-layer lower bounds add and separate copies attain their sum. This is a state-count result, not a transition gate-cost bound.

For N=1 and L={0}, each of the two layers has one residual, so the sum is 2; a single state label suffices at both positions with position-dependent transitions. The repaired statement must count states layer-by-layer or impose disjoint labels across layers.

Direct construction and proof are included in the statement. It uses only the definition of residuals and one-hot encoding; it does not rely on unreviewed proof-state steps or claim a succinct construction from an MCSP circuit.
proved_step: statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION CIRCUITS. Let L⊆{0,1}^N. At depth t, let the states be the r_t distinct residual languages R_t(p)={z:pz∈L}. For each t<N and input bit b, the transition from these states to the r_{t+1} residual states has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most 2r_t r_{t+1} AND/OR gates, given one-hot state input. Thus all position-specific transitions have total size at most 2∑_{t=0}^{N−1}r_t r_{t+1}. Proof: For each depth-t residual R, its b-section {z:bz∈R} is a unique depth-(t+1) residual, so the transition is a well-defined function f_b:[r_t]→[r_{t+1}]. For each target state j, output the OR of the one-hot input bits i for which f_b(i)=j. Implement each selected term with an AND gate and its OR with at most one fewer OR gates than terms. Across targets there are r_t terms total, hence at most r_t AND and r_t OR gates, bounded by 2r_t≤2r_t r_{t+1} since r_{t+1}≥1. This produces the exact next one-hot state. Applying the construction independently at every layer and for both input bits gives the stated bound per bit-symbol transition and total.

evidence: This is a direct construction from the residual transition function and the exact fan-in-two OR tree count. A finite verification is requested independently across all languages of lengths 0 through 3, including empty and singleton target classes; it is sanity evidence only, not needed for the proof.
proved_step: statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITIONS WITH EXACT OR COST. Let L be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and let r_t be the number of distinct residuals after prefixes of length t. Encode each depth-t residual by a one-hot vector of length r_t. For each t<N and input bit b, the next one-hot vector is computable using at most max(r_t-1,0) fan-in-two OR gates; across both symbols and all positions the total is at most 2*sum_{t=0}^{N-1} max(r_t-1,0). Proof: each source residual has exactly one b-section, which is a depth-(t+1) residual. For each target coordinate j, OR together the source coordinates whose b-section is j. If k_j sources map to j, this uses max(k_j-1,0) OR gates (zero for empty, one for singleton). Since every source maps to exactly one target, sum_j k_j=r_t, and the total is sum_j max(k_j-1,0) <= max(r_t-1,0). The resulting vector is exactly one-hot because each source one-hot vector maps to one target. Summing over b and t gives the bound. The empty language has one empty residual at every level and each transition is the identity on its sole one-hot coordinate, costing zero gates, also covered by the formula.

statement: EXPLICIT CIRCUIT-LIST PREFIX RECOGNIZER. Let A be the finite set of ordered fan-in-two Boolean circuit descriptions on n inputs with at most s gates, M=|A|. Maintain q_C in {0,1} for every C in A, initialized to 1. At position i, on bit b, update q_C := q_C AND [C(1,...,i-1,b,0,...,0)=b], where the bracket is the fixed truth-table bit of C at position i. Accept iff OR_{C in A} q_C=1. This recognizes exactly prefixes extendible to a truth table in A. Each position-specific transition takes at most M two-input AND gates and acceptance at most max(M-1,0) OR gates. If gate j has at most n+j available wires, then M <= sum_{k=0}^s product_{j=0}^{k-1}(2(n+j)^2+n+j+2).
derivation: For each C, induction on prefix length shows q_C=1 exactly when the first t truth-table bits of C equal the read prefix. The invariant holds at t=0. At the next position the update preserves q_C exactly when C's fixed truth-table bit there equals the received bit, proving the invariant at t+1. Therefore some q_C is 1 exactly when some listed circuit extends the prefix. The transition uses one AND per C with a position-and-circuit-dependent constant. The acceptance OR uses a binary tree. To bound M, count each exact gate count k by encoding each gate as one of two binary operations on an ordered pair of at most n+j wires, one of n+j wires, or one of two constants; sum these products for k=0 through s. This is an explicit-list construction only and gives no polynomial-in-s bound.

statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION CIRCUIT. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At level t<N, let R_t be the distinct residual sets R_t(p)={z: pz in F}, and let d_t=|R_t|. With one-hot input encoding of R in R_t, the map (R,b) -> R_b={u: bu in R}, encoded in R_{t+1}, is computed correctly on valid states by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 4d_t gates, with constants free.
derivation: For each source R in R_t and bit b, let dest(R,b)=R_b in R_{t+1}. For each destination S and bit b, form g_{S,b}=OR_{R:dest(R,b)=S} e_R, using a binary OR tree; empty groups yield constant 0. Since each source has exactly one destination for each b, the total number of OR gates across all groups for a fixed b is at most d_t, and across both b values at most 2d_t. Form h_{S,b}=g_{S,b} AND [input bit equals b], using at most 2d_{t+1} gates naively, but only destinations reached by at least one source need a gate; their count for each b is at most d_t, hence at most 2d_t such gates. Finally y_S=h_{S,0} OR h_{S,1}, using at most d_{t+1} gates, and d_{t+1}<=2d_t because every next-level residual is a section of some level-t residual, each of which has two sections. Total is at most 2d_t+2d_t+2d_t=6d_t, so the asserted 4d_t bound needs refinement. A valid bound of 6d_t follows from this construction. On a valid one-hot input exactly one source R is active, so exactly the coordinate for R_b is output as 1. Therefore replace the stated 4d_t bound with 6d_t before treating the claim as established.
scope: Canonical residual automaton of an arbitrary finite language at one fixed level, with one-hot state encoding and fixed level-dependent transitions. Does not bound d_t in terms of circuit size and does not give a representation map from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

statement: Corrected one-hot residual transition bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and let R_t be the distinct residuals after length-t prefixes, with d_t=|R_t|. The transition (R,b)->R_b, encoded one-hot, is computable on valid states by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most 7d_t gates, counting NOT gates and treating constants and wires as free.
derivation: For each destination S in R_{t+1} and bit b, let E_{S,b}={R in R_t:R_b=S}. Form g_{S,b}=OR_{R in E_{S,b}} e_R, using zero for an empty group. Across all (S,b), the OR trees use at most 2d_t gates, since each source contributes exactly one edge for each bit and an OR tree on k inputs uses at most k-1 gates. Form h_{S,b}=g_{S,b} AND (b=b), where the bit literal is b for b=1 and NOT b for b=0. The groups with nonempty E_{S,b} number at most 2d_t, so these AND gates cost at most 2d_t; one shared NOT gate supplies NOT b. For every S, output y_S=h_{S,0} OR h_{S,1}, using d_{t+1} gates. Every next-level residual is a section of a previous residual, so d_{t+1}<=2d_t. Total is at most 2d_t+2d_t+1+2d_t=6d_t+1<=7d_t, since d_t>=1. On a valid one-hot input exactly one source coordinate is active, so exactly the coordinate for R_b is output. This proves the corrected bound; it does not imply a bound on d_t from a circuit description or a transition simulation for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
scope: All finite nonempty languages F subseteq {0,1}^N, levels t<N, and valid one-hot state inputs. Fan-in-two AND/OR and unary NOT gates are counted; constants and wires are free. The construction is level-specific. No MCSP transfer or arbitrary-encoding lower bound is claimed.

proved_step: statement: WITNESS-ENUMERATION EXT STREAMING LEMMA. Let r,h,N be nonnegative integers and let H_i:{0,1}^r->{0,1} for i=1,...,N each be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most h gates. Let L={x in {0,1}^N: exists w in {0,1}^r such that x_i=H_i(w) for every i}. There is an exact deterministic prefix recognizer for L with 2^r state bits and, at position i, a transition circuit of at most O(2^r(h+1)) gates; the initial state is all ones and acceptance is the OR of the state bits. Proof: index state bits q_w by all w in {0,1}^r. At each position i, set q'_w=q_w AND (x_i iff H_i(w)). Compute H_i(w) with a separate copy of its at-most-h-gate circuit for each w, then combine with x_i and prior q_w using O(1) gates per w. Inductively, after t bits q_w=1 exactly when the first t bits equal H_1(w),...,H_t(w); hence some q_w remains 1 iff the prefix extends to a word in L. The accepting OR uses O(2^r) gates. This is an explicit transition-cost upper bound for a witness relation; it does not imply a lower bound or a relation to an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit C.

evidence: The argument is constructive: every gate contributes a constant-size local relation; topological induction proves the witness vector is the unique gate evaluation; fixing prefix bits adds no gates; and writing the suffix as b z' proves the child identity. The existential quantifiers remain in the conclusion, so no claim about their circuit-elimination cost is used.

statement: FIXED-CIRCUIT LOCAL VERIFIER AND PREFIX PROJECTION. Let C be a Boolean circuit with N input bits, h fan-in-two gates in topological order, and one output. There is a {AND,OR,NOT} circuit H_C(x,y), with O(h) gates, where y lists one bit per gate, such that H_C(x,y)=1 iff y gives the consistent gate evaluation of C on x and the output is 1. For any prefix p of length t and next bit b, define E_C(p)=1 iff there exist z in {0,1}^{N-t} and y with H_C(pz,y)=1. Then E_C(pb)=1 iff there exist z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} and y with H_C(pb z',y)=1. The relation circuit in the latter expression is obtained by substituting the fixed prefix bits in H_C, so it has no more gates than H_C. Proof: For each gate i, its local condition y_i=f_i(a_i,b_i) is a Boolean relation on at most three bits and therefore has a constant-size {AND,OR,NOT} circuit. Conjoin the h local conditions and the assertion that the output wire is 1 using O(h) additional gates. By induction in topological order, the local conditions force y to be exactly the circuit evaluation, so H_C accepts precisely accepting computations. Substituting fixed input bits adds no gates. Finally, write the remaining suffix as b z'; this gives the stated child projection identity. This lemma only constructs the local verifier and its exact prefix projection; it gives no small ordinary circuit for eliminating the existential variables and no transition-cost bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Use constant-size local Boolean constraints for each fan-in-two gate, conjoin them and the accepting-output constraint, then use topological induction for correctness. Input substitution preserves gate count, and suffix decomposition yields the child identity.
scope: All finite N and h; fixed fan-in-two Boolean circuit; existential projection is semantic and is not asserted to have a small Boolean circuit.

statement: FINITE EXHAUSTIVE CHECK OF EXISTENTIAL COFACTOR IDENTITY. For all Boolean relations H:{0,1}^2×{0,1}→{0,1}, every prefix p of length t<2, next bit b, and remaining suffix z, the projected predicate L(x)=∃w H(x,w) satisfies L(pb z)=∃w H(pb z,w). The exhaustive check enumerates all 256 relations and all prefix/bit/suffix cases. This is finite verification of the identity only, not a gate-complexity result or a general proof.
derivation: For each enumerated relation, define L(x) by existentially checking both possible witness values. For every tested p,b,z, the left side evaluates L on the concatenated string pbz, while the right side evaluates the same relation H on that same string for each witness and takes their disjunction. Thus the comparison checks the actual projection, rather than two independently written expressions. Exhaustion covers all Boolean relations on these domains and all indicated prefixes. The finite conclusion is exactly limited to n=2,r=1.

statement: EXPLICIT WITNESS-ENUMERATION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and input wiring free, and let G(x)=∨_{w∈{0,1}^r}H(x,w). Then G has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)−1 gates. For any fixed prefix p, the cofactor G_p has a circuit within the same bound, and fixing a further input bit to form G_{pb} adds no gates.
derivation: For each of the 2^r assignments w, make a separate copy of the h-gate circuit H and hardwire its witness inputs to w; this computes x↦H(x,w) using at most h gates. Combine the 2^r branch outputs with a binary OR tree, which uses 2^r−1 fan-in-two OR gates. Thus the total is at most 2^r h+(2^r−1)=2^r(h+1)−1. Hardwiring any visible input prefix into this circuit preserves its function on the remaining inputs and cannot increase its gate count. Hardwiring the next input bit likewise yields the next cofactor without adding gates. The argument proves an explicit exponential upper bound and makes no polynomial-size assertion when r grows.

evidence: Independent finite verification cm-d5bf8a16f70c460a checked 164 AND/OR/NOT circuits with up to two gates on two inputs; every tableau projection matched direct evaluation. This is a finite encoding check, not the proof of the general lemma.

statement: FIXED-CIRCUIT TABLEAU PROJECTION LEMMA. Let C be a fixed acyclic Boolean circuit with g fan-in-at-most-two gates in topological order, and let y_1,...,y_g be Boolean variables for its gate outputs. Let H_C(x,y) assert the correct local Boolean equation for every gate and that C's output is 1. Then for every input x, there is exactly one y satisfying all gate equations, and ∃y H_C(x,y)=1 iff C(x)=1. H_C has size O(g) in fan-in-two Boolean gates when constants and wiring are free. Proof: Induct on gate order. Once x and y_1,...,y_{i-1} are fixed, gate i's local equation forces y_i to its uniquely determined Boolean output. Thus exactly one y satisfies all gate equations, and it is C's evaluation tableau. Adding the output condition makes H_C satisfiable over y exactly when that tableau's output is 1. Each gate equation has constant-size Boolean implementation, and a binary AND tree combines the g equations and output condition using O(g) gates. This applies to one fixed deterministic circuit; it does not bound the cost of searching over candidate circuits for EXT or implement an EXT residual transition from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
derivation: For each input x, gate equations in topological order uniquely determine y_i, so exactly one tableau satisfies them. The output condition holds on that tableau exactly when C(x)=1. Local gate constraints have constant-size implementations and their conjunction uses a linear-size binary AND tree.
scope: Fixed acyclic fan-in-two Boolean circuit; existential variables encode only its internal gate outputs. The bound is O(g) and does not cover quantification over circuit descriptions.

gap: The transition cost for EXT_{n,s} requires existentially quantifying over all circuits C with |C|≤s. S0744 establishes cofactor computation for a FIXED circuit C, giving no bound on the search over circuit descriptions. For a prefix p, the EXT residue is determined by whether ∃C (size≤s) such that C extends p - this requires Σ_3^T-style reasoning beyond the witnessed cofactor construction. A transition algorithm would need to either: (1) avoid explicit circuit enumeration via a more direct characterization, or (2) prove that the existential search over circuits of size s can be done with poly(s) operations on some canonical representation of H_C.

The transition algorithm for EXT_{n,s} must handle the UNION over all circuits C with |C|≤s: T(x) = ⋁_{|C|≤s} H_C(x, ·). Even if each H_C has size poly(n) for fixed s, the number of such C is 2^{Ω(s)}, and their union structure cannot be compressed to poly(s) states by S0743 construction.
refuted_approach: The WITNESS-ELIMINATION LEMMA S0743 applies to transforming a single circuit H, not to the union of exponentially many tableau relations. The MMW19 algorithm uses Σ_3SAT oracle because EXT involves existential quantification over circuits; explicit enumeration would require 2^{Ω(s)} time.

evidence: The proof claims 'The pair (R_0,R_1) determines R, so d_t <= d_{t+1}^2'. This is invalid: while a level-t residual R determines its sections R_0 and R_1 (level-(t+1) residuals), the converse mapping from pairs (X,Y) of level-(t+1) residuals to level-t residuals is not injective. Multiple distinct level-t residuals can yield the same pair (R_0,R_1) when R_0 = R_1 (e.g., R = {0u, 1u} vs R = {0u} for same u). Computational check on all F subseteq {0,1}^n for n=3,4 shows the inequalities d_t <= d_{t+1}^2 and d_{t+1} <= 2d_t hold (0 violations), but the GIVEN PROOF does not establish them. The step is REFUTED due to invalid proof structure.

The construction is correct: for each string a_j, state bit q_j tracks whether the read prefix matches a_j's prefix. Initially q_j=1 (empty prefix matches all). Update q'_j = q_j AND [a_j(i)=b] correctly maintains the invariant: q_j=1 iff the read prefix equals the first i bits of a_j. Acceptance OR_j q_j = 1 iff at least one a_j extends the read prefix. Cost analysis: per position, M two-input AND gates (one per string with the constant [a_j(i)=b]); acceptance uses at most M-1 two-input OR gates in a binary tree. Total O(MN) gates for N positions. The construction handles M=0 (rejects all) and repeated strings correctly. No counterexample exists; the proof is valid.

proved_step:
statement: GATE-TRANSCRIPT PROJECTION LEMMA. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with m gates over AND, OR, and NOT, with primary input x and output wire o. Introduce one witness bit y_i for each gate output, in topological order. There is a fan-in-two circuit H_C(x,y) of O(m) gates that accepts exactly when every y_i equals the value of gate i on its predecessor wires and y_o=1. For every x there is exactly one gate-consistent transcript y, and C(x)=1 iff there exists y such that H_C(x,y)=1. Proof: For each gate i, a constant-size Boolean subcircuit checks equality between y_i and the AND, OR, or NOT of the at most two predecessor wires. A binary tree conjoins all consistency checks and the output bit, giving O(m) gates. Topological induction forces y_1, then y_2, and so on, uniquely to their gate values. The resulting transcript has y_o=C(x), so the conjunction is satisfiable exactly when C(x)=1.
proof: For each gate i construct a constant-size local equality check. Conjoin the m checks and output bit in a binary tree. Topological induction establishes uniqueness of the consistent transcript; its output wire equals C(x).

statement: FINITE-LANGUAGE PREFIX RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N, and for each t in {0,...,N} and each p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in L}. Then the number of distinct nonempty sets among {R_p: p in {0,1}^t} is at most min(2^t, |L|). If the empty set is counted as a residual, the number of distinct residuals is at most min(2^t, |L|)+1. Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so at most 2^t distinct residuals of any kind. For each prefix p with R_p nonempty, choose one z_p in R_p. The map p -> pz_p is injective because its output has prefix p; hence the number of prefixes with nonempty residual is at most |L|. The number of distinct nonempty residual sets is no greater than the number of prefixes with nonempty residuals, proving the bound. The empty residual contributes at most one additional set. This lemma applies to L=Im(Eval_{n,s}) and bounds the canonical prefix automaton's distinct nonempty states at each fixed depth by min(2^t, |Im(Eval_{n,s})|); it does not bound transition circuit cost or give a polynomial bound in n,s.
derivation: Fix t. Let P_t={p in {0,1}^t:R_p is nonempty}. For each p in P_t, choose z_p with pz_p in L. If p≠q, then pz_p≠qz_q because their first t bits differ. Thus p↦pz_p is an injection P_t→L and |P_t|≤|L|. The number of distinct nonempty residuals is ≤|P_t|, and also ≤2^t. Adding the single possible empty residual yields the stated bound.

gap: The gate-transcript projection lemma does not establish that EXT automaton transitions can be implemented by a bounded number of operations on H_C with real gate costs, nor that any such representation applies to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits. Need a construction/proof connecting the prefix-extension language to H_C, or a precise obstruction and a repaired enriched representation.

statement: LITERAL PREFIX-REGISTER UPDATE LEMMA (restricted model). For any Boolean relation H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1}, store the observed prefix p in a register and retain H unchanged. On input bit b, update (p,H) to (pb,H). The represented residual after this update is exactly z' |-> exists w H(pb z',w). The update uses no Boolean gates only when register append/copy is the primitive transition operation; it stores t+1 prefix bits after t+1 inputs. This construction proves no transition-circuit bound when the next encoded state must be computed by a fan-in-two circuit.
derivation: Define R_p(z)=1 iff exists w H(pz,w). For every z', R_{pb}(z')=1 iff exists w H(pb z',w)=R_p(bz'), so the updated register represents the exact next residual. The state update itself appends b to p and leaves H unchanged. Under a register-write cost model this is a primitive update; under a Boolean-circuit cost model the register must be encoded and computed, so no zero-gate conclusion follows.

evidence: Direct finite-description construction and proof above; no computation is needed for this combinatorial bound. The result gives an explicit, generally exponential-in-s representation, not the O(s log(n+s))-bit EXT automaton state or a real-gate transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
proved_step: statement: CANDIDATE-SET RESIDUAL LEMMA. Fix n,s and the standard fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit model with constants and wires free, and let F be the finite set of descriptions of circuits on n inputs with at most s gates (designated output included). For p∈{0,1}^t, define A_p={D∈F: Eval_D(x_i)=p_i for every i<t}, where x_0,…,x_{2^n−1} is the fixed truth-table input order. Then EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff A_p is nonempty, and A_{pb}={D∈A_p: Eval_D(x_t)=b}. If M=|F|, this state is represented by M bits and its update can be performed by testing each candidate circuit on x_t, in O(Ms) gate evaluations; M≤(s+1)(3(n+2s+2)^2)^s under a padded description encoding. Proof: by definition, D∈A_p exactly when its first t truth-table outputs equal p, so there exists a size-≤s circuit with prefix p iff A_p is nonempty. Appending b requires agreement on the first t positions and output b at position t, giving the displayed update equality in both directions. A circuit with j≤s ordered gates is described by at most 3 choices of gate type and at most (n+2s+2)^2 ordered source choices per gate, with at most s+1 choices for the designated output; summing j=0,…,s is bounded by the stated M. Testing one description on one input takes O(s) gate evaluations, so scanning the M-bit candidate vector costs O(Ms). This is an exact sufficient representation and update bound; it neither proves that the M-bit state is necessary nor provides a compact transition implementation.

evidence: Direct set-theoretic proof for all finite indexed function families; no enumeration used. This isolates the cost of combining a supplied viability mask with the candidate set, without claiming the mask is cheap to construct.
proved_step: statement: For any finite indexed family F=(f_1,...,f_M) of Boolean functions on {0,1}^N and prefix p of length t<N, define B_p={i: there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t} with f_i(pz)=1}. For b in {0,1}, define A_{p,b}={i: there exists z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} with f_i(pb z')=1}. Then B_{pb}=B_p ∩ A_{p,b}. Therefore, given M-bit characteristic vectors for B_p and A_{p,b}, the update is coordinatewise AND and uses M two-input AND gates. This excludes the cost of constructing A_{p,b}. Proof: if i∈B_{pb}, a witnessing suffix z' yields suffix bz' for B_p, hence i∈B_p and i∈A_{p,b}. Conversely, i∈A_{p,b} has a suffix witnessing i∈B_{pb}; intersection with B_p does not remove it. Thus equality holds.

evidence: For each of the 2^k suffixes z, substitute b and z into a separate copy of f_i, leaving u as input. Each copy uses at most s gates. OR the 2^k outputs using a binary tree of 2^k-1 gates. This computes the existential disjunction exactly. Summing over M candidates gives the stated total. This is an upper bound only and is exponential in k.
proved_step: statement: Let each f_i:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most s gates. For a prefix length t<N and bit b, put k=N-t-1 and define V_{i,b}(u)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^k with f_i(ubz)=1, for u in {0,1}^t. Then V_{i,b} has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^k(s+1)-1 gates. Consequently, for M candidates all M viability predicates have circuits with at most M(2^k(s+1)-1) gates in total; evaluating at p supplies A_{p,b}, after which B_p is updated with M AND gates.

evidence: Direct coordinatewise construction and fan-in-two gate accounting; no computation required. Scope is the explicit candidate-description vector for EXT, not arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
proved_step: statement: EXPLICIT CANDIDATE-SET TRANSITION CIRCUIT. Fix n,s, a finite circuit-description set F of size M, an input x_t, and a bit b. Let q_D indicate whether description D remains consistent with the prefix before x_t. The updated indicator is q'_D=q_D AND [Eval_D(x_t)=b] for every D∈F. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit computing q' from q with at most c M(s+1) gates for an absolute constant c, when each D has at most s gates and x_t is fixed; the circuit is constructible from (F,x_t,b) in O(Ms) time. Proof: For each D, unroll its at-most-s gate computation on the fixed input x_t into a Boolean circuit of at most c0(s+1) gates, obtaining the constant e_D=Eval_D(x_t). If e_D≠b, set q'_D=0 using a constant output; if e_D=b, wire q'_D directly to q_D. This already gives a circuit with no more than M wires and constants under the convention that constants and wiring are free. Under a stricter gate-only encoding with no free constants, use one shared constant generator and one AND gate per D to compute q_D AND [e_D=b], costing at most M+O(1) gates. Alternatively, if x_t is supplied as variable input rather than fixed, unroll each D's evaluation using at most c0(s+1) gates and compare its output to b and AND with q_D, using O(s+1) gates per D, hence at most cM(s+1). Correctness is coordinatewise: q'_D=1 exactly when q_D=1 and D outputs b on x_t, precisely the consistency condition after appending b. This is an explicit transition circuit for the candidate-set representation; its state dimension M may be exponential in s log(n+s), so it gives no compact-state result.

evidence: Direct continuation-separation proof for deterministic exact streaming algorithms. Independent of the unreviewed candidate-set claims S0830 and S0833. No computation used; no transition circuit or arbitrary-MCSP bridge is asserted.
proved_step: statement: FIXED-POSITION RESIDUAL SEPARATION. Let L be any Boolean language on strings of a fixed length N, and for each t let R_p(z)=L(pz) for prefixes p of length t and suffixes z of length N-t. Let K_t be the number of distinct functions R_p. Every deterministic exact streaming algorithm deciding L must have at least K_t distinct internal configurations after t input bits; if configurations are encoded in fixed-length binary using b_t bits, then b_t >= ceil(log_2 K_t). Proof: Assume prefixes p,q of length t have the same configuration but R_p and R_q differ. Then there exists a suffix z with L(pz) != L(qz). Determinism and equality of the configurations imply that processing the common continuation z yields the same final answer from both prefixes, contradicting exactness. Thus each distinct residual function requires a distinct configuration. For L equal to the length-N prefix-extension language of EXT_{n,s}, this applies with R_p(z)=EXT_{n,s}(pz). This gives a necessary information bound only; it does not bound K_t or the real-gate cost of transitions.

evidence: For any i in B_p, a witnessing suffix z has first bit b and remainder z', so i belongs to A_{p,b}. Conversely, membership in either A_{p,b} supplies a witnessing suffix bz' for B_p. This proves the union equality. The child equality is immediate since its defining prefix is pb.
proved_step: statement: For any finite indexed family F=(f_1,...,f_M) of Boolean functions on {0,1}^N and any prefix p of length t<N, define B_p={i: exists z in {0,1}^{N-t} with f_i(pz)=1}. For b in {0,1}, define A_{p,b}={i: exists z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} with f_i(pb z')=1}. Then B_p=A_{p,0} union A_{p,1}, and B_{pb}=A_{p,b}.

proved_step: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY EXT RESIDUAL UPDATE LEMMA. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be an explicitly listed family of pairwise distinct functions f_i:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, represented by their truth tables in a fixed coordinate order. For a prefix p of length t, define A_p={i : f_i[1..t]=p} and R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t} : there exists i in A_p with f_i[t+1..N]=u}. For b in {0,1}, define A_{pb}={i in A_p : f_i[t+1]=b}. Then (i) A_{pb} is exactly the live-candidate set after reading b, (ii) R_{pb}={v : there exists i in A_{pb} with f_i[t+2..N]=v}, and (iii) the map i -> f_i[t+1..N] is injective on A_p. Given the explicit truth tables, A_{pb} is computed by scanning A_p and testing one bit per candidate, in O(M) time. Proof: By definitions, i belongs to A_{pb} iff f_i agrees with p and its next bit is b, exactly the condition that i survives the next prefix; the suffix set of those surviving candidates is the displayed R_{pb}. If i,j in A_p have the same remaining suffix, they also agree on the prefix p, so their full truth tables are equal, and pairwise distinctness implies i=j. A scan of at most M candidates performs one next-bit test per candidate and outputs exactly A_{pb}, taking O(M) time under an explicit-list representation. This is a finite-family representation/update lemma; it asserts no polynomial-in-s transition from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

evidence: The displayed equivalence proves exactness for every suffix and witness. The circuit is unchanged; only the stored prefix grows by one bit. This is a representation lemma and makes no claim that the projected residual has a compact Boolean circuit.
proved_step: statement: Let H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r -> {0,1} be a Boolean circuit with h gates, and define L(x)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1. Represent the residual after prefix p by (H,p), with residual L_p(z)=1 iff exists w H(pz,w)=1. On reading b, update (H,p) to (H,pb). This represents L_{pb}(z)=L_p(bz) exactly, leaves H at h gates, and stores at most N prefix bits. Proof: for every suffix z, L_{pb}(z)=1 iff exists w H(pbz,w)=1 iff L_p(bz)=1. The update appends b to p and does not change H.

evidence: The proof is a direct count of ordered circuit descriptions in the stated fixed basis. Every projected residual at a fixed level has a cofactored witness-relation circuit of at most h gates; counting those circuits upper-bounds the number of projections.
proved_step: statement: Fix a Boolean circuit basis with q gate types of fan-in at most two, where constants and input wiring are free. Let H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r -> {0,1} have at most h gates, and define L(x)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1. For each fixed prefix length t, the number of distinct residual functions L_p(z)=L(pz), over p in {0,1}^t, is at most q^h (N+r+h+2)^(2h+1). By the definition of I_p, i belongs to I_{pb} exactly when it belongs to I_p and its t-th truth-table bit equals b, so these outputs are exactly the new membership vector. Proof: Choose one representative witness w_j from each of the d equivalence classes under f_w=f_{w'}. For each representative, substitute w_j into a copy of H, obtaining f_{w_j} with at most h gates. OR the d outputs with a binary tree using d−1 gates. For each x, this OR is 1 iff at least one representative class has H(x,w_j)=1; since each class has identical f_w, this is equivalent to ∃w H(x,w)=1. Thus the size is at most dh+d−1=d(h+1)−1. Fixing prefix coordinates in the resulting circuit cannot increase the number of gates, proving the cofactor statements. statement: PREFIXWISE DISTINCT-COFACTOR PROJECTION BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} have a fan-in-two circuit with h gates. Then the projected residual L_p(z)=∨_{w}H(pz,w) is computed by a fan-in-two circuit with at most d_p(h+1)−1 gates. After reading bit b, every member of F_{pb} is obtained by cofactoring some member of F_p at its first suffix input; therefore d_{pb}≤d_p, and this representation can be updated by cofactoring each retained function and removing duplicates. Proof: For each f∈F_p, take one circuit computing f and OR the d_p outputs using d_p−1 gates. Repeated witness functions do not change this OR, proving the size bound. For any suffix z', L_{pb}(z')=∨_w H(pb z',w)=∨_w H(p(bz'),w)=L_p(bz'). Also each function z'↦H(pb z',w) is the cofactor at b of z↦H(pz,w), so the distinct set at pb is a subset of the cofactored images of F_p and has size at most d_p. This is a representation-size bound only: identifying equal cofactors may require expensive computation, and the bound does not give a compact update algorithm for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: For fixed n,s, let F_{n,s} be the length-N truth tables computed by circuits of size at most s. For every prefix p let R_p={z:pz in F_{n,s}}. The minimum number of states of a deterministic automaton recognizing the prefix language of F_{n,s} is D=|{R_p:p a prefix}|; consequently any exact state encoding requires at least ceil(log2 D) bits.
proof: If R_p=R_q, every suffix is accepted after p iff it is accepted after q, so merging them preserves the language. If R_p differs from R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference; then exactly one of pz,qz belongs to F_{n,s}, so merging p,q misclassifies one. Therefore equality of completion sets is precisely the indistinguishability equivalence, and its D classes are necessary and sufficient states. D distinct states require at least ceil(log2 D) bits.

For a finite family F⊆{0,1}^N, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−|p|}: pz∈F} for every binary prefix p of length at most N. The minimum number of states in a deterministic automaton that recognizes exactly the prefixes of words in F is the number D of distinct sets R_p, including the empty set when it occurs. Proof: Each prefix p has residual language R_p. If R_p=R_q, then for each next bit b and each remaining suffix z, bz∈R_p iff bz∈R_q, so p and q have identical acceptance behavior for every continuation and may be merged. Conversely, if R_p≠R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference; the continuation z is accepted from exactly one of p,q, so any deterministic automaton recognizing the language must place them in different states. Thus the equivalence classes of prefixes under equality of residual languages are exactly the necessary and sufficient states, and their number is D.

statement: PREFIX-CLOSURE RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION. Let N≥0, F⊆{0,1}^N, P=Pref(F), and for p∈P let R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N−|p|}: pu∈F}. Let K_p={z∈{0,1}^{≤N−|p|}: pz∈P}. Then K_p=Pref(R_p): z∈K_p iff z is a prefix of some u∈R_p. Consequently K_p=K_q iff either |p|=|q| and R_p=R_q, or R_p=R_q=∅.
proof: For z of length at most N−|p|, pz∈P iff there exists y with pzy∈F, by prefix closure. This is equivalent to zy∈R_p for some y, meaning z is a prefix of an element of R_p. If R_p and R_q are nonempty at different depths, their words have different fixed lengths, so their prefix languages have different maximum word lengths. At equal depth, equality of R sets implies equality of prefix sets; conversely, elements of R_p have maximum remaining length and so are exactly the maximum-length elements of Pref(R_p), recovering R_p from that prefix language. Empty residuals yield the same empty continuation language at every depth. Myhill–Nerode then says precisely the equal continuation languages can be merged, while unequal ones are distinguished by a continuation in their symmetric difference.

WIRE-CONSISTENCY REPRESENTATION. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with g gates, topologically ordered, and output wire o. Introduce one bit w_i for each gate. Let H_C(y,w) assert, for every i, that w_i equals gate i applied to its input wires, and also assert o=1. Then H_C has O(g) fan-in-two gates, and C(y)=1 iff there exists w with H_C(y,w)=1. For every y, the gate equations force a unique w. Proof: Induct in topological order: each gate’s inputs are primary inputs or earlier gate outputs, so its equation uniquely sets w_i to the value computed by C. Thus the unique satisfying assignment to the gate equations is C’s evaluation; adding o=1 makes the existential projection accept exactly when C(y)=1. Each local equation has constant-size implementation and their conjunction uses O(g) gates. This representation does not bound the cost of updating or canonicalizing projected residuals.

MINIMAL EXACT RECOGNIZER STATES ARE RESIDUAL LANGUAGES. Let L be a language over a finite alphabet and let P be the set of prefixes under consideration. For p define R_p={z:pz∈L}. Every deterministic exact recognizer has distinct states after p and q whenever R_p≠R_q; conversely, the distinct residuals form the states of an exact recognizer, with transition R_p --a--> R_{pa} and acceptance iff the empty suffix belongs to the residual. Thus the minimum number of states reachable by prefixes in P is exactly the number of distinct residuals among P. Proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. A recognizer in the same state after p and q processes z identically, contradicting exactness. For the converse, define the transition by R_p→R_{pa}; it is well-defined because R_p=R_q implies for every a,z, az∈R_p iff az∈R_q, hence R_{pa}=R_{qa}. Also R_p is accepting exactly when ε∈R_p, which is equivalent to p∈L. This characterizes precisely the information any exact prefix recognizer must retain. It gives no lower bound on real-gate transition cost for H_C and no implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement_start: DISTINGUISHING-SUFFIX SIGNATURE LEMMA. Let U be a finite suffix set and let R_1,...,R_K be distinct subsets of U. For every unordered pair {i,j}, choose u_{ij} in the symmetric difference R_i triangle R_j. Define sigma(R_i) as its membership vector over the chosen suffixes. Then sigma is injective and uses at most binomial(K,2) coordinates. Conversely, any injective binary signature for these K residuals requires at least ceil(log_2 K) coordinates. Proof: For i != j, the selected u_{ij} belongs to exactly one of R_i,R_j, so their corresponding coordinate differs and sigma(R_i) != sigma(R_j). There are binomial(K,2) pairs, hence no more than that many chosen coordinates (duplicates can be removed). A q-coordinate binary vector has at most 2^q possible values, so injectivity implies K <= 2^q and q >= ceil(log_2 K). For K=0 or 1, the empty coordinate set is injective and the lower bound is zero. At an EXT prefix level, take U to be the set of all suffixes of the remaining length and the R_i to be its distinct residual languages; the same result applies exactly. This gives a finite separating feature set once the witnesses are selected, but does not construct the witnesses efficiently or bound update cost from H_C.

statement_start: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX RESIDUAL BOUND. For F subset {0,1}^N with |F|=M and 0<=t<=N, the number K_t of distinct residual sets F_p={z:pz in F}, p in {0,1}^t, is at most min(2^t,M)+1. Proof: there are 2^t prefixes. Every nonempty residual comes from an extendable prefix. Distinct extendable prefixes each contain a distinct member of F, so there are at most M such prefixes and at most M nonempty residuals. There is at most one additional empty residual. Thus K_t<=min(2^t,M)+1. The levelwise minimal deterministic residual automaton has at most sum_{t=0}^N (min(2^t,M)+1) states. The update after bit b is exactly F_{pb}={z:bz in F_p}, by definition. This finite-family bound does not bound real-gate transition cost for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or improve the known EXT bound when M is large.

statement_start: EXT DESCRIPTION-COUNT RESIDUAL BOUND. Fix n,s and a finite encoding of fan-in-two Boolean circuits of size at most s, with at most B distinct descriptions. Let F be the set of their N-bit truth tables, N=2^n. At every prefix length t, the number of distinct residual sets F_p={z:pz in F} is at most min(2^t,|F|)+1, hence at most B+1. Proof: There are 2^t prefixes. Every nonempty residual belongs to an extendable prefix; distinct extendable prefixes contain disjoint sets of full truth tables, so choosing one table from each gives at most |F| such prefixes. There is at most one empty residual. Also |F|<=B because each description computes one table. Thus the bound follows. Encoding each residual by its prefix-history trie state takes at most ceil(log2(B+1)) bits at a level, and its exact transition is residual R -> {z:bz in R}. This bounds the states needed for EXT from description count; it does not give bounded real-gate transitions for an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
