statement: Residual-trie construction. For any finite A subset {0,1}^N, let R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz in A}. At each depth t, use one state for each distinct nonempty R_p with |p|=t, plus a dead state. From state R_p on bit b, transition to R_{pb} if nonempty, otherwise dead; dead loops to itself. Accept at depth N exactly when the residual contains the empty string. This deterministic automaton recognizes A and has at most 1+sum_{t=0}^N D_t states, where D_t is the number of distinct nonempty residuals at depth t.
proof: For every prefix p represented by R_p, its continuation z is accepted exactly when z is in R_p, by definition. After reading b then suffix z, acceptance is equivalent to bz in R_p, which is equivalent to z in R_{pb}; if R_{pb} is empty no completion is in A and the dead state is correct. Distinct prefixes with the same residual therefore have identical future behavior, so identifying them is safe. At depth N, the only possible residual is {epsilon} for words in A, and the empty residual is represented by dead. Thus the stated state count and language recognition follow.

statement: Explicit candidate-set transition for EXT. Fix n and s, and let C be the finite set of fan-in-two circuit descriptions of size at most s over a fixed finite gate basis, with fixed encodings of inputs and output. For each prefix p of length t define S_p={D in C: Eval(D) has prefix p}. Then the residual EXT_{n,s}|p is nonempty exactly when S_p is nonempty. On reading bit b, S_{pb}={D in S_p: Eval(D)_{t+1}=b}. This representation admits an update circuit with O(M(n,s)(s+log(n+s))) fan-in-two gates, where M(n,s)=|C|, when the truth-table index is supplied in binary. This is an upper bound for this representation, not a lower bound or a transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
proof: For each D in C, evaluate its output on the input indexed by t+1. Its at-most-s gates can be evaluated using O(s) gates; decoding the binary index costs O(log(n+s)) under the stated model. Compare the output with b and AND that match bit with D's old membership bit in S_p. Parallelizing over M descriptions produces the membership vector for S_{pb} using O(M(s+log(n+s))) gates. A suffix z completes p to a word in Im(Eval) exactly when some D in S_p agrees with all bits of z, so S_p represents the residual exactly. Filtering by the next bit therefore gives the exact next candidate set and the stated cost.

statement: Fixed-position candidate-set update lemma. Fix n,s, a finite encoded family C of M Boolean circuits D:{0,1}^n->{0,1} of size at most s, and an ordering x_0,...,x_{2^n-1} of their truth-table inputs. For a length-t prefix p define u_p(D)=1 exactly when D(x_j)=p_j for every j<t. At level t, reading bit b updates the membership vector by u_{pb}(D)=u_p(D) AND [D(x_t)=b]. With the position t fixed by the level, this update is implementable by a fan-in-two circuit of at most M AND gates, with the constants [D(x_t)=b] hardwired. The representation uses M state bits. It is exact for EXT_{n,s}, but this bound is for the explicit candidate-set representation and makes no claim about compact state or transitions for an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
proof: By definition, D belongs to the candidate set after pb iff it agrees with p on all positions j<t and agrees with b at position t. The first condition is u_p(D)=1 and the second is the fixed Boolean constant [D(x_t)=b]. Their conjunction gives the displayed update independently for every D. Thus the updated vector represents exactly the circuits whose truth tables extend pb. A suffix completes pb to a truth table in the family iff at least one such circuit agrees with every remaining bit, so the represented candidate set determines the EXT residual exactly. Each output coordinate requires at most one AND gate when constants and wiring are free, giving at most M gates total.

statement: Candidate-set residual-count lemma. Fix n,s and a finite family C of M Boolean circuits D:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, with truth-table input order x_0,...,x_{2^n-1}. For each prefix p, let S_p={D in C: D agrees with p on its positions}. The number of distinct residual languages EXT_{n,s}|p, over all prefixes p at all levels, is at most 2^M. In particular, at any fixed level t it is at most min(2^t,2^M).
proof: For each prefix p define its residual R_p={z: there exists D in S_p whose outputs on the positions after p equal z}. Thus R_p is determined entirely by S_p: if S_p=S_q, then the same circuits remain and have the same remaining truth-table outputs, so R_p=R_q. There are at most 2^M subsets of C, hence at most 2^M distinct residual languages across all prefixes. At level t there are 2^t prefixes, giving the additional bound 2^t. This proves the claim. The bound is a representation-specific upper bound; it gives no lower bound on the number of states needed by other representations and no transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION BOUND. Let L be a language of binary strings of fixed length N. At depth t, let R_t be the set of distinct residual languages L_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}, over prefixes p of length t, and put r_t=|R_t|. For each residual R in R_t and bit b, its child is R_b={z: bz in R}, which lies in R_{t+1}. Encode a residual by its one-hot vector over R_t. The deterministic update on input b from layer t to t+1 has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most r_t-1 OR gates (besides free wires/constants), producing the one-hot child vector.
proof: For each Q in R_{t+1}, define its fiber F_Q={R in R_t: R_b=Q}. The output coordinate for Q is the OR of the input coordinates indexed by F_Q; this is exact because the input is one-hot and each residual has exactly one child. A fiber of size k>0 needs k-1 binary OR gates, and an empty fiber needs zero gates (constant 0). The nonempty fibers partition R_t, so summing their costs gives r_t-|im(child)|≤r_t-1, since R_t is nonempty and hence the image has at least one element. This constructs the update circuit and proves the bound.

proved_step: statement: BLOCK-CONTROLLED RESIDUAL TRANSITION LEMMA. Let L be a language of fixed-length binary strings, and at depth t let R_t be its r distinct residuals. For a block length k with t+k<=N, each block a in {0,1}^k induces a deterministic map f_a:R_t -> R_{t+k}, where f_a(R)={z: az in R}. If the block a is supplied as an external control (not computed by the transition circuit), then the one-hot encoding of R is updated exactly to the one-hot encoding of f_a(R) using at most r-1 fan-in-two OR gates. Proof: For each Q in R_{t+k}, let F_Q={R in R_t:f_a(R)=Q}. Output coordinate Q is the OR of input coordinates in F_Q (or constant 0 if empty). Since the input is one-hot, exactly the coordinate for f_a(R) is set. A fiber of size q costs max(q-1,0) OR gates. Nonempty fibers partition R_t, so total cost is r-|im(f_a)|<=r-1, since R_t is nonempty. This only bounds the controlled update; it does not include computing a or provide a compact canonical encoding.

statement: INPUT-CHARGED ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION. Let R and R' be nonempty finite sets, |R|=r, and let f_0,f_1:R→R' be arbitrary maps. In the circuit model with fan-in-two AND/OR and NOT gates all charged, a circuit taking a one-hot encoding x of an element of R and a bit b outputs the one-hot encoding of f_b(x) using at most 4r gates on valid one-hot inputs. Proof: Compute ¬b once. For each i∈R compute u_i=x_i∧b and v_i=x_i∧¬b, using 2r gates. For each j∈R', output y_j as the OR of all u_i with f_1(i)=j and all v_i with f_0(i)=j; an empty OR is constant 0. Across all outputs these term lists partition the 2r terms, so binary OR trees use at most 2r−1 gates. Total is 1+2r+(2r−1)=4r. For a valid one-hot x, exactly the term selected by b and its unique source coordinate is 1, and it appears at output f_b(i); hence outputs are exactly one-hot. This repairs the transition-cost statement with an explicit input convention and charged NOT gate. It concerns arbitrary finite transition maps and does not provide a compact encoding or a transition procedure for H_C / EXT.

statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY LOWER BOUND. Let L be any language of fixed-length strings {0,1}^N. For each t in {0,...,N}, let R_t={L_p:p in {0,1}^t}, where L_p(z)=1 iff pz is in L. Any deterministic one-pass streaming machine that, after reading each length-t prefix, stores a state from which it can correctly decide membership for every continuation z of length N-t must have at least |R_t| distinct states at level t. Proof: Suppose two prefixes p,q of length t with L_p != L_q led to the same state. Since the residual functions differ, there exists a suffix z of length N-t for which exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. Starting from the same state and then reading the same z forces a deterministic machine to produce the same final answer on both strings, contradicting correctness. Thus prefixes with distinct residuals must occupy distinct states, giving at least |R_t| states. In particular the state requires at least ceil(log2 |R_t|) bits. For EXT_{n,s}, this applies to the exact prefix language over truth-table strings, but by itself neither bounds |R_t| superpolynomially for the relevant threshold nor charges the cost of deriving transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

statement: RESIDUAL-TABLE TRANSITION LEMMA. For L⊆{0,1}^N and prefix p, let T_p be the lexicographically ordered truth table of z↦1[pz∈L]. For b∈{0,1}, T_{pb}[z]=T_p[bz] for every suffix z; hence T_{pb} is the b-indexed half of T_p and the transition is coordinate selection, using zero Boolean gates when wires and output selection are free. If a level has D distinct residual functions, any deterministic exact state encoding with a decoder needs at least log₂D bits.
proof: For each suffix z, T_{pb}[z]=1 iff pbz∈L iff T_p[bz]=1, proving the transition identity and half-table description. Distinct residual functions differ on some suffix, so an exact deterministic decoder cannot assign them the same state; D states require at least log₂D bits.

statement: RESIDUAL COUNTING LEMMA. Fix a finite Boolean gate basis of size g and a standard fan-in-two circuit model with N input bits and h gates. Let D_t be the number of distinct residual functions L_p(z)=L(pz) over prefixes p of length t, where L is computed by such a circuit. Then D_t ≤ min(2^t, (g(N+h+2)^2)^h (N+h+1)) for h≥1; for h=0, D_t≤min(2^t,N+1).
proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so D_t≤2^t. Each residual is computed by the original circuit after fixing t input wires, hence by a circuit with at most h gates and at most N remaining inputs. To count descriptions, order the gates topologically. For each gate choose one of g types and two incoming wires from at most N+h+2 available inputs or earlier gates; choose one output wire from at most N+h+1 wires. Thus the number of descriptions is at most (g(N+h+2)^2)^h(N+h+1), which bounds the number of functions represented. If h=0, the output is an input or a constant, giving at most N+1 functions. Combining the two bounds proves the claim.

statement: WITNESS-ELIMINATION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. Then G(x)=1 iff there exists w∈{0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)-1 gates. For every prefix p of x, the cofactor G_p has a circuit with no more than this bound.
proof: For each w∈{0,1}^r, copy the h-gate circuit H and substitute the constants of w on its witness inputs. The resulting circuit computes x↦H(x,w) and uses at most h gates. OR the 2^r outputs with a binary tree, which uses 2^r−1 gates. The total is at most 2^r h +(2^r−1)=2^r(h+1)−1, and this computes G by existential semantics. Fixing the coordinates of any prefix p by input substitution cannot increase the gate count, giving the same bound for G_p.

statement: DISTINCT-WITNESS-SLICE ELIMINATION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two circuit with h gates. For each w define H_w(x)=H(x,w), and let q be the number of distinct Boolean functions among {H_w : w∈{0,1}^r}. Then G(x)=1 iff ∃w H(x,w)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit with at most q(h+1)-1 gates. Every prefix cofactor of G has a circuit within the same bound.
proof: Choose one representative witness w_i for each of the q distinct functions H_w. For each representative, copy H and substitute the constants w_i on its witness inputs; this computes H_{w_i} with at most h gates. OR the q outputs with a binary tree of q−1 OR gates. The resulting circuit computes G, since duplicate slices do not change an OR and every witness assignment belongs to one represented slice. Its size is at most qh+(q−1)=q(h+1)-1. Fixing the input coordinates of any prefix cofactor cannot increase circuit size, so the same bound holds for every prefix.

statement: COFACTOR MONOTONICITY OF DISTINCT WITNESS SLICES. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1}. For a prefix p of length t, let q_p be the number of distinct functions z↦H(pz,w), as w ranges over {0,1}^r. For every next bit b, q_{pb}≤q_p. Consequently, if H has a fan-in-two circuit with h gates, the existential projection G_p(z)=∃w H(pz,w) has a fan-in-two circuit of at most q_p(h+1)-1 gates at every prefix, and this bound never increases along a path.
proof: For each witness w, write f_w(z)=H(pz,w). Its child slice is f_{w,b}(z')=H(pbz',w)=f_w(bz'), the cofactor of f_w obtained by fixing its first input to b. If f_w=f_{w'} as functions on all suffixes z, then f_w(bz')=f_{w'}(bz') for every z'; hence the map from parent slice classes to child slice classes is well-defined and surjective onto the set of child classes. Therefore q_{pb}≤q_p. Applying the distinct-slice elimination construction to the child relation yields a circuit for G_{pb} of size at most q_{pb}(h+1)-1, which is no larger than q_p(h+1)-1. The same argument applies at every prefix, including the empty and full prefixes.

evidence: The step is mathematically correct. Cofactoring a circuit by fixing prefix bits to constants (input substitution) does not increase gate count and can only decrease it via constant propagation. The existential quantifier over witness bits w∈{0,1}^r is unchanged. The identity R_{pb}(z') = R_p(bz') holds by string concatenation: pb z' = p(bz'). This is a valid representation/update lemma about exact cofactoring of witness relations. No counterexample exists.

The construction is mathematically correct and standard. For each of the 2^r witness values w, substitute w into a copy of H (≤ h gates per copy). Combine the 2^r outputs with a binary OR tree (2^r − 1 fan-in-2 OR gates). Total gates = 2^r·h + (2^r − 1) = 2^r(h+1) − 1. Cofactoring by prefix p substitutes constants into x-inputs, which never increases gate count (constant propagation can only reduce it). The step correctly notes this is exponential in r and does not claim a polynomial bound. No counterexample exists.

Correct. Substituting constants for the prefix x-bits (and fixing the next z-input to b) never increases the fan-in-2 gate count (wiring substitution; constant propagation only reduces it), so H_{pb} has ≤ h gates. The equality L_{pb}={v:bv∈L_p} is immediate from ∃w H(pbv,w)=1 ⇔ bv∈L_p, with the same witness domain {0,1}^r. The step is explicitly a representation/update lemma and disclaims compactness/canonicalization, so there is no overclaim. No counterexample found.

proved_step: PACKED EXPLICIT TRANSITION TABLE LEMMA. Let D={0,1}^k be a set of d=2^k state codes and let T:D×{0,1}→D be any fixed transition table. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(dk) gates computing T(q,b) on every q∈D and b∈{0,1}. Proof: For each u∈D form selector e_u=[q=u], using k input literals and a binary AND tree, with at most O(k) gates per u. For output coordinate j, form the OR of e_u AND [T(u,b)_j=1] over all (u,b) pairs, additionally selecting the corresponding input bit b; equivalently use selectors [q=u] AND [b=β] for each pair (u,β). There are 2d selectors, each costing O(k), and at most 2dk selector-to-output incidences, whose OR trees cost O(dk) total. The output bits therefore equal T(q,b) for every valid code q. Padding unused codes with arbitrary transitions gives a total circuit. The bound concerns a known nonuniform table and does not include the cost of constructing that table or converting an EXT state from an H_C representation.

FINITE-IMAGE RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let F be a finite subset of {0,1}^N with |F|=M. For each t in {0,...,N} and p in {0,1}^t, define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. At each level t there are at most M+1 distinct residuals, and across all levels there are at most (N+1)(M+1) level-tagged residual states. Proof: Fix t. Every nonempty residual R_t(p) has a witness z with pz in F. For distinct prefixes p,p' of length t, the sets of strings extending them are disjoint. Choose one prefix and one witness for each distinct nonempty residual. These witnesses are distinct: if two chosen witnesses were the same string, its length-t prefix would determine the same prefix and hence the same residual. Thus there are at most M nonempty residuals. The empty residual contributes at most one more. Summing over the N+1 levels gives at most (N+1)(M+1) level-tagged states. They can be assigned binary labels of length ceil(log2((N+1)(M+1))). This is only a state-count and encoding bound; it gives no efficient way to compute labels or transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

lemma: Explicit-candidate residual update lemma: Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean words of common length N. At level t, store a∈{0,1}^M with a_j=1 exactly when f_j[0:t]=p. On reading b, update a_j' = a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. This update is computable in at most M+1 fan-in-two gates and produces exactly the state for pb. Proof: for every j, a_j'=1 iff f_j[0:t]=p and f_j(t)=b, iff f_j[0:t+1]=pb. At a fixed level, f_j(t) is a constant. Use a_j AND b when it is 1, and a_j AND NOT b when it is 0, sharing one NOT gate. Thus at most M+1 gates; M=0 is immediate. The state uses M bits and constants require the explicit list. No bound follows for exponentially many candidate circuits or for conversion from arbitrary H_C.

statement: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE FILTER UPDATE LEMMA. For every N,M≥0 and every explicitly listed family F=(f_1,...,f_M)⊆{0,1}^N, define a prefix-agreement state a∈{0,1}^M at level t by a_j=1 iff f_j[0:t]=p. For each t<N and next bit b, the coordinate update a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b] produces exactly the agreement state for pb and is computable by a nonuniform fan-in-two circuit of at most M+1 gates. The lemma holds for empty families and all prefixes, including t=0 and t=N−1.
proof: For each j, a'_j=1 iff a_j=1 and f_j(t)=b. By the definition of a_j, this is equivalent to f_j[0:t]=p and f_j(t)=b, which is equivalent to f_j[0:t+1]=pb. Thus the output vector is exactly the prefix-agreement vector at level t+1. At a fixed level the bits f_j(t) are constants. If the constant is 1, the coordinate is a_j AND b; if it is 0, it is a_j AND NOT b. Share one NOT b gate across all coordinates, and use one AND gate per coordinate, for at most M+1 gates. For M=0 no coordinate gates are needed. At t=N−1 the resulting vector marks exactly the listed words equal to the full word pb. This proof makes no claim about compressing the M-bit state or computing it from an arbitrary decision circuit H_C.

evidence: The lemma correctly bounds the number of distinct residual sets: at each level t, there are at most M+1 distinct residuals (M nonempty ones witnessed by distinct elements of F, plus possibly the empty residual). The total number of level-tagged states is at most (N+1)(M+1). The bound is tight: for F being all 2^N strings, M=2^N and at t=0 there are exactly 2^N distinct residuals. For F being exactly one string, M=1 and the bound still holds. The argument is sound.

proved_step: EXPLICIT-LIST AGREEMENT UPDATE LEMMA. Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be a listed family of distinct bit strings of length N. At level t encode prefix p by a_j=1 iff f_j begins with p. On reading b, set a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. This is exact and costs at most M fan-in-two gates, since each [f_j(t)=b] is a level-specific constant. The vector identifies the listed strings compatible with p and hence their suffix set. Proof: For every j, a'_j=1 iff f_j begins with p and its next bit equals b, iff f_j begins with pb. Therefore the updated vector is exactly the agreement vector for pb. Each coordinate is a constant, wire, or one AND gate. This applies only to an explicit listed family and gives no polynomial-in-s transition bound for succinct circuit families or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

evidence: The agreement vector does update in O(M) gates, but the asserted O(M log(M+1)) translation from an arbitrary packed residual code to that vector is unsupported. An arbitrary lookup from log D code bits to M output bits has no such general bound: its truth table may require order MD/log(MD) gates. Thus the packed-code conversion claim fails. Retaining the M-bit agreement vector, as in S0755, repairs the explicit-list transition claim.

proved_step: EXPLICIT-EXT UPDATE BOUND. Fix n,s and an explicit list F of all distinct truth tables computed by fan-in-two Boolean circuits with n inputs and at most s gates, under any fixed circuit encoding. Let M=|F|. The prefix survivor-vector transition for EXT_{n,s} is exact and uses at most M fan-in-two gates per input bit. Proof: Index the tables f_1,...,f_M. At level t store a_j=1 iff f_j agrees with the current prefix on its first t positions. On reading bit b, set a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. The bracket is a level-specific constant, so each coordinate needs at most one AND gate. Thus a' records exactly the tables agreeing with the extended prefix. Initially all coordinates are 1, and induction proves the invariant at every level. This is a nonuniform explicit-list construction; its transition bound is M and does not imply poly(s,n) cost because the list may be exponentially large in s log(n+s).

statement: For F={0,1}^N, the survivor vectors of distinct length-t prefixes are pairwise distinct; hence any injective binary encoding of all reachable survivor states at level t requires at least t bits.
derivation: For a prefix p, let a_p(x)=1 iff x begins with p, for each x in F. If p and q are distinct length-t strings, choose any x extending p; then a_p(x)=1 and a_q(x)=0. Thus p↦a_p is injective on the 2^t prefixes. An injective encoding of 2^t states by B bits requires 2^B≥2^t, so B≥t.
scope: Integers N≥t≥0; F is the explicit set of every N-bit Boolean string; survivor state is the incidence vector indexed by F; binary encoding is required to be injective on reachable states.

proved_step: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY PREFIX UPDATE (independent proof attempt). Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be an explicitly listed family of binary strings of common length N. After prefix p, store a_j=1 iff f_j begins with p. On reading bit b, define a'_j=a_j if the (|p|+1)-st bit of f_j equals b, and a'_j=0 otherwise. Then a' encodes exactly the members of F beginning with pb. Proof: For each j, a'_j=1 iff a_j=1 and f_j[|p|+1]=b, which holds iff f_j begins with p and has next bit b, equivalently iff f_j begins with pb. Each output is a wire from a_j or constant zero, so the Boolean gate cost is zero when wiring/constants are free. All transitions can be constructed by scanning the explicit family in O(MN) time. This gives no polynomial bound for implicit circuit families.

Establishing or refuting a comparable poly(s) transition representation for implicit EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits remains open; G0004 is not closed.
proved_step: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY BINARY RESIDUAL AUTOMATON. Let F be an explicitly listed set of M distinct strings in {0,1}^N. For each level t, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. There are at most M+1 distinct residuals at level t: the empty set and at most M nonempty residuals. Indeed, if two nonempty residuals R_t(p),R_t(p') intersect, some f in F has both p and p' as its length-t prefix, hence p=p' and the residuals are equal. Index the distinct residuals at each level by 0,...,d_t-1, where d_t<=M+1, and encode an index in k=ceil(log2(M+1)) bits (with the trivial M=0 case handled by one state). For each level, the transition function on a valid state index and input bit b is a Boolean function on at most 2(M+1) input pairs, with output the index of the b-section {u:bu in R}; such a section is exactly the next-level residual reached by appending b. Extend the function arbitrarily to invalid codes. A multiplexer tree over the k+1 input bits computes each output bit with O(2^(k+1))=O(M+1) fan-in-two gates, so the transition circuit uses O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates. Given the explicit list, all level residual indices and transition tables are constructible by scanning the strings and their prefixes. This is an exact construction for explicit F only; since M may be exponential in the circuit-size parameter for the implicit family of small circuits, it gives no poly(s) transition bound and does not close G0004.

proved_step: statement: SHARED TSEITIN ENCODING FOR ALL EXT PREFIX QUERIES. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with N input bits and s gates, and introduce one variable y_g for each gate g. There is a CNF formula T_C(x,y) with O(s) clauses and O(s) variables such that, for every input x, C(x)=1 iff there exists y satisfying T_C(x,y) together with the unit clause requiring the output gate to be 1. For each prefix p of length t<N and bit b, EXT_C(pb)=1 iff the same T_C, together with output=1 and the t+1 unit assumptions x_1=p_1,...,x_t=p_t,x_{t+1}=b, is satisfiable. Thus one encoding of C is shared across all prefix transitions; each transition changes only the prefix assumptions, adding one unit assumption. Proof: For each gate, encode its Boolean truth-table relation between its input wires and output wire by a constant number of clauses; conjoin these clauses over all gates and require the output wire to be 1. Given x, the circuit's unique gate evaluation supplies a satisfying y exactly when C(x)=1, and any satisfying y must agree with that evaluation gate by gate in topological order. For a fixed prefix, the remaining input variables are existentially free, so satisfiability of the stated CNF under the prefix units is equivalent to the existence of an accepting completion. The construction uses O(s) clauses and variables and is independent of the chosen prefix. This yields a shared existential-CNF representation of EXT transitions, but does not give a deterministic bounded-gate transition circuit after eliminating the free input and gate variables, nor a reduction to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: SURVIVOR-MASK EXTENSION LEMMA. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a finite indexed family of Boolean strings of length N, with each f_j explicitly available. At prefix length t, let A(p)={j:f_j[1..t]=p}. The mask m(p) in {0,1}^M whose jth bit is 1 iff j is in A(p) is an exact representation of EXT_F(p): EXT_F(p)=1 iff |A(p)|>0. Given m(p) and next bit b, the mask m(pb) is computed by M fan-in-two gates, one per index, since m'_j=m_j AND [f_j[t+1]=b], where bracket is a hardwired constant. For all prefixes and all t<N, induction gives the invariant that m(p) marks exactly the family members extending p. Consequently, after preprocessing the explicit family, the entire EXT_F automaton has a deterministic transition circuit of size M at each level and uses M state bits; preprocessing time is O(MN). Proof: At t=0 all indices extend the empty prefix. Assuming the invariant at p, index j extends pb iff it extends p and its (t+1)st bit equals b. This is precisely the displayed update. Induction proves exactness. The output bit is the OR of the M mask bits, so acceptance is also computable in at most M-1 additional gates. The representation and cost are explicit-family bounds; they do not imply a polynomial-size transition on a succinct circuit description of the family or on arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Induction on prefix length using the coordinatewise filter; the per-coordinate predicate is constant after fixing the explicit family and level.

evidence: The claim correctly establishes that for the literal-prefix representation (H,p), the transition (H,p) -> (H,pb) is exact with zero additional gates in H. Proof: L_{pb}(v) = 1 iff exists w H(pbv,w) = 1 = L_p(bv) by definition of L_p. The transition only appends b to stored prefix p; H is unchanged so gate count remains h. This is a valid lemma about this representation, though explicitly not compact (stores t+1 prefix bits). No counterexample exists - the argument is mathematically sound for the stated representation.

The one-hot transition construction is mathematically correct. For any subset F, the residuals at consecutive levels are well-defined. Given one-hot encoding q of R_i at level t, the child residual R_i^b = {u : bu in R_i} is exactly one of the level-(t+1) residuals U_j. The construction a_ib = q_i AND b (or NOT b) followed by q'_j = OR of a_ib with j(i,b)=j correctly computes the one-hot encoding at level t+1. The gate count is at most 2d conjunctions + at most 2d OR gates (binary trees), so O(d+e) is correct. Verified by explicit construction on the even-parity example (F={000,011,101,110}) where d=2, e=2 and transitions work perfectly. The lemma correctly notes this applies to canonical one-hot states, not compressed encodings.

Verified construction: for explicit list of M strings, transition uses at most M AND gates (each a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]). The bracket is hardwired constant 0/1, so this is correct. The invariant a_j=1 iff f_j agrees with prefix on first t coordinates holds by induction. Example verified on F={000,011,101,110}.

Checked the standard NP witness verification construction: given circuit C of size s, prefix p of length t, bit b, the witness (q,y) where q in {0,1}^{N-t-1} is the suffix and y in {0,1}^s is the gate tableau. The verifier checks each gate equation in topological order, checks output gate = 1, and checks fixed prefix bits match p and b. Each gate check is constant-size Boolean circuitry; conjunction over s gates costs O(s); prefix/witness wiring costs O(N). If EXT_C(pb)=1, an accepting completion q exists and its uniquely induced tableau y makes the verifier accept. Conversely, an accepting verifier assignment yields a completion on which C outputs 1. No argument gap found; this is a correct polynomial-size nondeterministic representation of the EXT transition predicate.

The update rule q'_C = q_C AND [w_C(t)=b] correctly maintains the set of circuits whose output begins with the extended prefix pb. A circuit matches pb iff it matched p and its t-th output bit equals b. Since w_C(t) is hardwired for each candidate, the comparison is a constant (b or NOT b) and one AND gate per candidate suffices. The lemma explicitly acknowledges no compact-state bound (mask has one bit per description). No logical gap or counterexample found.

This is a standard Myhill-Nerode argument for layered deterministic streaming automata. The proof is correct: (1) A deterministic left-to-right streaming decider has a state set Q_t at each level t, a deterministic transition function delta_t: Q_t x {0,1} -> Q_{t+1}, and an output function out: Q_N -> {0,1}. (2) The state after reading prefix p determines the entire future behavior: for any continuation z, the computation from state q on z is uniquely determined by delta. (3) If p and q reach the same state q_t in Q_t, then for every z, the final state reached is identical, so out(final state) is identical. (4) If R_t(p) != R_t(q), there exists z in the symmetric difference where exactly one of pz, qz is in L. But the decider gives the same answer on both, contradicting exactness. (5) Therefore R_t(p) = R_t(q), and the number of distinct states at level t is at least the number of distinct residuals. No counterexample exists because this follows directly from the definition of a deterministic streaming decider. The step correctly notes this gives an information-theoretic state lower bound but no real-gate transition-cost bound or arbitrary MCSP circuit transfer.

This construction is correct. It explicitly enumerates all M circuit descriptions of size ≤ s. The invariant: v_p[j] = 1 iff circuit C_j is consistent with all prefix bits seen so far (i.e., C_j(x_i) = p_i for all i < t). Base case t=0: v_ε[j] = 1 for all j (all circuits consistent with empty prefix). Inductive step: when reading bit b at position t, v_{pb}[j] = v_p[j] ∧ [C_j(x_t) = b]. This exactly maintains the invariant because a circuit remains consistent with prefix pb iff it was consistent with p AND outputs b on the t-th input x_t. At t=N, v_p[j]=1 iff C_j's full truth table equals p, so EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff ∃j: v_p[j]=1. The update is a fan-in-2 circuit: each coordinate is an AND of the previous bit and a hardwired constant (the circuit's output on x_t), so O(M) gates per update; computing C_j(x_t) for all j takes O(M(s+n)) with the descriptions hardwired. The step correctly notes this does not yield polynomial-in-s transition cost (M is exponential in s) and no transfer to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits. No counterexample exists - this is a direct explicit construction.

This is a correct characterization of the residuals for EXT_{n,s}. Proof: z ∈ R_t(p) ⇔ pz ∈ EXT_{n,s} ⇔ ∃C ∈ C_s such that C's truth table = pz ⇔ C ∈ A_p and T_C^(t) = z. So R_t(p) = {T_C^(t) : C ∈ A_p} exactly. Two prefixes p,q have equal residuals iff {T_C^(t) : C ∈ A_p} = {T_C^(t) : C ∈ A_q} as sets of suffix tables. The cardinality bound: there are at most 2^{|C_s|} distinct subsets of C_s (each yielding a set of suffix tables), and at most 2^{2^{N-t}} distinct subsets of {0,1}^{N-t}. The min of these is a valid upper bound. The step correctly notes this gives a semantic quotient of the candidate-filter state but no compact representation or real-gate transition bound. No counterexample - this follows directly from the definitions.

The argument is a standard Myhill-Nerode style proof for streaming recognizers. If two prefixes have distinct residual sets, there exists a distinguishing suffix z in their symmetric difference. Determinism forces identical states to produce identical outputs on the same suffix, contradicting exact recognition. The injection from residual classes to states is valid. No counterexample exists - this is a fundamental fact about deterministic automata. The step correctly notes this gives only a state-count (workspace) lower bound, not a transition-circuit or update-time bound.

This directly follows from S0767: the injection from d_t residual classes to machine states implies at least d_t distinct states. With S state bits, at most 2^S states are representable, so 2^S >= d_t, giving S >= ceil(log2 d_t). This is the standard space lower bound for deterministic streaming recognition (the log of the number of Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes at layer t). The step correctly restricts the claim to workspace only.

This is a restatement of the core Myhill-Nerode argument for streaming deciders, identical in substance to S0767 and S0768. The logic is sound: distinct residuals imply a distinguishing suffix; determinism forces equal states to yield equal outputs on that suffix, contradicting exact decision. The conclusion that at least d_t states are needed is correct.

The construction is correct: given the explicit residual transition table tau_b: D_t -> D_{t+1}, the one-hot transition circuit computes the next one-hot state. For each target Q and input bit b, g_{Q,b} is the OR of one-hot sources that transition to Q on b; since the input encoding is valid one-hot, exactly one source is active, so g_{Q,b} correctly indicates whether the transition leads to Q. The output selector o_Q = (not b AND g_{Q,0}) OR (b AND g_{Q,1}) chooses the correct b-branch. Gate count: each of the 2d_t source-bit occurrences appears in exactly one OR tree (total <= 2d_t gates for all ORs); each of the d_{t+1} targets uses at most 3 gates (two ANDs and one OR) plus one shared NOT for b. Total <= 2d_t + 3d_{t+1} + 1 <= 3d_t + 3d_{t+1}. The step correctly notes this is for one-hot encoding with explicit transition table, not for compressed encodings.

The construction correctly implements the transition function on valid binary codes. Decoding each source code to a one-hot indicator I_a takes O(k) gates per source (AND of k literals or constant 1). Grouping by successor via OR trees: each of the d sources appears in exactly one OR per bit b, so total OR gates O(d+e). Selecting the branch with b costs O(e) gates (NOT b, two ANDs, one OR per target). Re-encoding the one-hot target to l-bit binary: for each of l output bits, OR the H_q where that bit of code(q) is 1, costing O(e*l + l). Sum: O(d(k+1) + d + e + e*l + l) = O(d(k+1) + e(l+1)). The circuit is correct on valid inputs; invalid inputs are unspecified as stated. No counterexample - this is a standard explicit decoding/transition/encoding construction.

The construction is correct: maintaining the exact set of live witnesses as an M-bit vector, the update filters by the next required output bit. Since y_{i,t} is a fixed constant for each candidate i and position t, the test [y_{i,t}=b] is either b (if y=1) or NOT b (if y=0). Each updated bit is z_i AND (b or NOT b), which is a single fan-in-2 gate per candidate (plus one shared NOT). This correctly computes S_{t+1}(pb). The state is empty iff no witness matches the prefix. This is an explicit exponential-state construction (M = number of circuits), correctly noted as not bounding compressed encodings.

The argument is correct linear algebra over GF(2). The set of prefixes with nonempty residuals is exactly the preimage of c+im(D) under phi(p)=Pp+im(D). This is either empty (if c+im(D) not in im(phi)) or an affine subspace p0+ker(phi). For p in this affine subspace, the residual R(p) is the solution set of Dz = c-Pp. Two such fibers are equal iff their right-hand sides agree, i.e., Pp1 = Pp2. Thus distinct nonempty residuals correspond exactly to distinct values of Pp over p in p0+ker(phi), which is the image P(ker(phi)), of size 2^rank(P|ker(phi)). This is an exact characterization for affine languages.

The construction is correct: for each of d_t residuals R and each bit b, the token q_{R,b} = x_R AND l_b (where l_1=b, l_0=NOT b) uses 2d_t AND gates and 1 NOT gate. Each R' in D_{t+1} receives the OR of tokens whose section R_b equals R'; these tokens partition the 2d_t tokens. Binary OR trees over each partition use at most 2d_t total gates. Total <= 4d_t+1 <= 6d_t+1. The step correctly limits its scope to the one-hot representation and does not claim bounds on d_t for EXT or general MCSP circuits.

The proof is correct: each prefix p maps to a configuration c(p). If c(p)=c(q), then determinism + fixed oracle O implies identical future behavior on all suffixes z, so R_t(p)=R_t(q). The proof is correct: splitting Ax=c gives A_<t p + D_+ z = c, so D_+ z = c + A_<t p over GF(2). The mapping p -> c + A_<t p has at most 2^r values, each determining a residual. The update y(pb) = c + A_<t(pb) = c + A_<t p + b*a_t = y(p) + b*a_t uses r conditional XORs (O(r) fan-in-2 gates). Correct for affine languages only.

Correct: f_i has prefix pb iff f_i has prefix p AND its t-th coordinate equals b. The residual characterization follows directly. Update uses M AND gates with constant selectors. Correct. This is a straightforward combinatorial construction: the vector q_p tracks which of the M explicit words match prefix p. The OR of q_p checks whether any word matches p (extendability). Correct. This is the standard Myhill-Nerode / residual distinguishability argument for deterministic streaming automata. If two prefixes p,q reach the same state, then for any suffix z the computation on pz and qz must be identical (same final state, same output). Exact decision means the output equals membership in F, so pz in F iff qz in F for all z, meaning R_t(p)=R_t(q). Contrapositive: distinct residuals require distinct states. The workspace bound ceil(log2 d_t) bits follows immediately. The lemma correctly states its scope: it gives a state-space lower bound, not an update-time bound, and does not evaluate d_t for EXT_{n,s}. No counterexample exists for this general information-theoretic fact.

Correct. The linear algebra is sound: D_+z = b has a solution iff b is orthogonal to ker(D_+^T), i.e., V^T b = 0. Here b = c + A_<t p + b a_t. The number of parity equations is rank(V) = dim(ker(D_+^T)) = r - rank(D_+) <= r. Each parity involves at most t+1 bits of p plus the constant b. Fan-in-two XOR tree computes each parity in O(t+1) gates; AND of r parities uses O(r) gates. The O(1) boundary accounts for empty systems (r=0) where V is empty and the condition is vacuously true (0 equations = satisfied). This correctly bounds the circuit cost for affine GF(2) suffix projection. The scope limitation is properly stated: it does not apply to EXT or H_C transitions.

Computational verification on all languages up to N=4 (100 random languages per N plus structured languages: empty, full, parity, first-bit) confirms: (1) the transition map from depth-t residual class [p] and bit b to depth-(t+1) class [pb] is well-defined, with residual exactly the b-section of R_t(p); (2) equal parent residuals imply equal child residuals (representative-independence); (3) distinct residuals require distinct states. Verified the inductive construction: for a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with fixed topological order, each gate's output is uniquely determined by its inputs (input bits x or earlier witness bits y_{<i}). The conjunction H_C(x,y) = (y_o=1) ∧ ⋀_i (y_i = gate_i(x, y_{<i})) has exactly one satisfying y for each x, namely the evaluation trace. H_C(x,y)=1 iff C(x)=1 and y is that trace. Fixing a prefix p substitutes constants into input wires, yielding H_{C,p}(z,y) = H_C(pz,y) with the same unique-trace property. The existential projection ∃y H_{C,p}(z,y) equals C(pz). No logical gap found; the step correctly establishes exact cofactoring without claiming bounds on compiling the projection.

Verified the construction: for a finite Boolean language L ⊆ {0,1}^N, the residuals R_t(p) = {z ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} : pz ∈ L} for |p|=t are well-defined. Setting W = max_t r_t and injecting residuals at each depth t into [W] via c_t gives a deterministic length-N recognizer with position-dependent transitions. The transition c_t(R) → c_{t+1}(R_b) where R_b = {z : bz ∈ R} is well-defined because R_b is a function of R. Terminal acceptance at depth N (accept iff ε ∈ R) correctly recognizes L. The converse (two distinct residuals at same depth cannot share a state) holds because a distinguishing suffix would then be accepted identically, contradicting distinctness. The step correctly bounds state labels only and makes no claim about gate cost for succinct transitions.

Verified the construction: For each of the 2^k assignments a to the k suffix bits z, substitute constants on those input wires in the original fan-in-two circuit C. This yields 2^k circuits C_a(u) each of size at most g (substitution does not add gates). The predicate P(u) = OR_{a in {0,1}^k} C_a(u) is exactly the existential projection. Combining the 2^k outputs with a binary OR tree uses 2^k - 1 additional fan-in-two gates. Total size <= 2^k * g + 2^k - 1. The construction is correct, uniform given C and k, and preserves fan-in-two. The scope notes correctly state this gives no polynomial bound when k grows (exponential in k), and no conclusion for MCSP when k is large. No counterexample exists; the argument is a standard enumeration-of-suffixes construction.

Verified the construction: Given a fan-in-two circuit H with h gates computing H(x,w) where x∈{0,1}^N, w∈{0,1}^r. For a fixed prefix p∈{0,1}^t, substitute the constant values of p into the first t input wires of H. This yields a circuit H_p with the same gate structure (at most h gates) computing H(pz,w) for z∈{0,1}^{N-t}, w∈{0,1}^r. Substitution of constants cannot increase gate count—it only replaces input wires with constants, possibly simplifying some gates to constants. The relation L_p(z) = ∃w H_p(z,w) = 1 is exactly the residual language after prefix p by definition: {z : ∃w H(pz,w)=1} = {z : pz ∈ L}. Fixing an additional bit b gives H_{pb} by one more constant substitution, again ≤ h gates. The lemma correctly states this bounds the cofactor circuit size only, not the projected language L_p itself (which would require eliminating the existential quantifier over w). No counterexample exists; this is a standard circuit restriction fact.

Verified the construction step by step: (1) For each v∈{0,1}^k, cofactor H by fixing k suffix inputs - substitution preserves gate count ≤ h. (2) OR-combination of 2^k predicates via binary tree uses 2^k-1 gates. (3) Total ≤ 2^k*h + 2^k - 1 ≤ 2^k(h+k+1). (4) For k ≤ c*log₂(h+2), we have 2^k ≤ (h+2)^c, giving polynomial size. The construction is correct, uniform, and the bounds are tight. Scope note correctly states this bounds one fixed circuit H, not the existential set of all candidate circuits. Checked on small cases: h=2, k=1 gives at most 2*(2+1+1)=8 gates, which matches direct enumeration. No counterexample exists; this is a standard cofactor-OR construction.

Verified the construction: (1) For each of the 2^k assignments a to witness bit z, substitute constants into circuit C, yielding C_a(u) with ≤ g gates each (substitution preserves gate structure). (2) The predicate P(u) = ∨_a C_a(u) is computed by OR-ing 2^k output bits using a binary OR tree requiring 2^k - 1 additional gates. (3) Total gate count ≤ 2^k * g + 2^k - 1. Construction verified: for each output coordinate j (S total), function f_j: {0,1}^{S+1} -> {0,1} built via truth-table DNF. At most 2^{S+1} minterms, each AND of S+1 literals (S AND gates), S+1 shared NOT gates, OR tree of 2^{S+1}-1 gates. Per-coordinate: (S+2)2^{S+1}-1 gates. Total: S(S+2)2^{S+1}-S <= S(S+2)2^{S+1}. Standard constructive upper bound, no gap. Explicitly does not address cost of obtaining transition tables from H_C.

The construction is correct: for each of the 2^r witness assignments w, substitute the fixed prefix p and w into H, yielding a circuit H_{p,w}(z) on the remaining inputs with at most h gates (fixing inputs never increases gate count in a fan-in-two circuit). Combine the 2^r outputs with a binary OR tree of 2^r-1 fan-in-two OR gates. The resulting circuit computes the existential quantification exactly, has fan-in two throughout, and size at most 2^r h + 2^r - 1. No counterexample exists; this is a standard valid upper-bound construction. The claim explicitly states it is an upper bound, not a lower bound, and makes no P≠NP progress claim.

This follows directly from S0798 (which survived review). S0798 gives size ≤ 2^r h + 2^r - 1. The hypothesis r ≤ c log2(h) implies 2^r ≤ h^c. Substituting: size ≤ h^c · h + h^c = h^(c+1) + h^c. The derivation is algebraically correct and the polynomial bound in h for fixed c is correctly stated. No gap or counterexample.

This restates S0799 with a self-contained proof that does not depend on earlier steps. The proof constructs the same circuit: 2^r copies of H with substituted constants, combined by a binary OR tree. Size ≤ 2^r h + 2^r - 1. With r ≤ c log2(h), 2^r ≤ h^c, giving h^(c+1) + h^c. The construction and arithmetic are correct. It correctly notes this is a polynomial upper bound only in the logarithmic-witness regime and makes no lower-bound or P≠NP claim.

The proof is correct: each prefix p of length t defines an index set I_p = {j : a_j begins with p}. Distinct prefixes have disjoint index sets. There are at most M nonempty such sets (since the M strings partition into at most M nonempty groups) plus at most one empty set (for prefixes extending no string in A). Also there are at most 2^t prefixes total. Hence r_t ≤ min(2^t, M+1). Summing the looser bound M+1 over N+1 depths gives the stated total bound. This is a purely combinatorial fact about listed multisets, independent of circuit representations. No counterexample exists.

Asymptotic bound error: the construction costs r_t*ceil(log2 r_t) gates for equality decoding plus 2*r_t*ceil(log2 r_{t+1}) for OR trees plus ceil(log2 r_{t+1}) for selection = O(r_t log r_t + r_t log r_{t+1}). The claim O(r_t log r_{t+1}) assumes log r_t = O(log r_{t+1}), but r_{t+1} <= 2r_t only gives an upper bound, not a lower bound. Counterexample regime: r_t = 1024, r_{t+1} = 2. Then actual cost ~ 1024*10 + 1024*1 = 11264 gates, but claimed bound O(r_t log r_{t+1}) = O(1024*1) = 1024, off by factor ~11. The boundary case claim 'constant-width boundary cases take O(r_t) gates' also fails when r_t is large but r_{t+1} is constant. S0804 repairs this by keeping both logarithmic factors.

Construction verified: (1) Equality decoding for each of r_t legal indices uses O(ceil(log2 r_t)) fan-in-2 gates per index (AND tree comparing against fixed binary code), total O(r_t ceil(log2 r_t)). (2) For each of 2 input bits b and ceil(log2 r_{t+1}) output bits k, OR the equality indicators of indices i with table entry output bit k = 1 on b; each OR costs O(r_t) gates, total O(2 * r_t * ceil(log2 r_{t+1})) = O(r_t ceil(log2 r_{t+1})). (3) Bit-controlled selection between the two branch outputs uses O(ceil(log2 r_{t+1})) mux gates. Sum = O(r_t ceil(log2 r_t) + r_t ceil(log2 r_{t+1}) + ceil(log2 r_{t+1})). The repaired bound correctly retains both logarithmic factors, fixing S0802's error. No counterexample found for the stated construction.

Mathematical verification: R_{pb}(z) = 1 iff ∃w H(pbz, w) = 1. By associativity of string concatenation, pbz = p(bz). Thus ∃w H(p(bz), w) = 1, which is exactly R_p(bz) = 1. The identity holds by definition of R_p and associativity of concatenation; the existential witness domain is identical on both sides. No counterexample exists - this is a tautological identity over finite strings.

Mathematical verification of the explicit algorithm: (1) Evaluation: for fixed p,z, iterate over all 2^r witness strings w∈{0,1}^r, evaluate the h-gate circuit H on input (pz,w). Accept iff any evaluation outputs 1. This uses exactly 2^r circuit evaluations, each evaluating at most h gates, so ≤ 2^r h gate evaluations total. (2) Working space: the read-only circuit description (h gates) plus storage for current witness w (r bits), current suffix z (≤N bits), gate values during one evaluation (h bits), and loop counters = O(h+N+r) bits. (3) Transition identity: R_{pb}(z') = 1 ⇔ ∃w H(pb z', w) = 1 ⇔ ∃w H(p(bz'), w) = 1 ⇔ R_p(bz') = 1 by associativity of concatenation. The bounds are worst-case upper bounds attained by the explicit enumeration algorithm; no counterexample exists for this constructive claim.

Mathematical verification: (1) Lower bound: at depth t, distinct residuals R_t(p) ≠ R_t(p') are distinguished by some suffix z, so any exact automaton needs different states for them. Thus ≥ r_t states at depth t, so ≥ max_t r_t states overall. With disjoint layer copies, the lower bounds add, giving ≥ Σ_t r_t. (2) Upper bound (shared): let R = max_t r_t. Assign each residual at each layer a unique code from [R]. For each layer t and bit b, transition from code of A to code of A_b = {z : bz ∈ A}. This is well-defined since A determines both sections. Induction: after reading prefix p, state = code of R_t(p); acceptance is exact. (3) Upper bound (disjoint): use separate codes per layer, sum = Σ_t r_t. Construction is explicit. No counterexample - this is a standard Myhill-Nerode / residual automaton result for position-dependent (layered) automata.

Mathematical verification of the one-hot construction: (1) States at depth t are one-hot vectors of length r_t. (2) For each b, the transition function f_b: [r_t] -> [r_{t+1}] is well-defined because each residual R has a unique b-section R_b = {z : bz in R} which is a depth-(t+1) residual. (3) To compute output coordinate j, OR together all input coordinates i where f_b(i)=j. If k_j sources map to j, this uses k_j AND gates (each AND-ing the one-hot input bit with constant 1, effectively just passing it) and max(k_j-1, 0) OR gates. Since sum_j k_j = r_t, total AND gates = r_t, total OR gates <= r_t - 1 < r_t. So total gates per (t,b) <= 2r_t. Since r_{t+1} >= 1, 2r_t <= 2r_t r_{t+1}. The construction is explicit and exact. No counterexample exists.

Mathematical verification of the optimized one-hot construction: (1) States are one-hot vectors of length r_t. (2) For fixed b, each source residual i has exactly one b-section, which maps to a unique target j = f_b(i). (3) To compute output coordinate j, we OR together the k_j source coordinates mapping to j. If k_j >= 2, this uses k_j - 1 OR gates (fan-in-2, binary tree). If k_j = 1, 0 gates needed (just wire). If k_j = 0, 0 gates (constant 0). Total OR gates = sum_j max(k_j - 1, 0). Since sum_j k_j = r_t and each k_j >= 0, the maximum of this sum is when one k_j = r_t and others = 0, giving max(r_t - 1, 0). Per bit b: <= max(r_t - 1, 0) OR gates. Two bits per layer: <= 2 * max(r_t - 1, 0). Sum over t = 0 to N-1 gives the bound. The empty language case (r_t = 1 for all t) gives max(0,0) = 0 gates, covered by formula. No AND gates needed since one-hot input directly selects sources. Construction is explicit and exact. No counterexample exists.

The update rule is mathematically incorrect. The claim states: q_C := q_C AND [C(1,...,i-1,b,0,...,0) = b] where the bracket is described as 'the fixed truth-table bit of C at position i'. However, C(1,...,i-1,b,0,...,0) evaluates circuit C on an n-bit input where the first i-1 bits are 1, the i-th bit is b, and the rest are 0. This is NOT the i-th bit of C's truth table (which has length 2^n and is indexed by all n-bit strings in lexicographic order). The truth table bit at position i is a fixed constant for each circuit C (the value of C on the i-th input string), not a function of the input bit b being read. The correct update would be q_C := q_C AND [T_C[i] == b] where T_C is the precomputed truth table of C. The written rule confuses truth table positions with circuit inputs and makes the transition depend on b in the wrong way. This error invalidates the claimed construction.

The derivation itself identifies a flaw: the construction yields at most 6d_t gates, not 4d_t as stated. The step counts: (1) g_{S,b} = OR of sources mapping to S for bit b: total OR gates across both bits <= 2d_t (since each of d_t sources has exactly one destination per bit, sum of k_j = d_t per bit). (2) h_{S,b} = g_{S,b} AND [input bit = b]: at most 2d_t gates (only destinations reached need gates, at most d_t per bit). (3) y_S = h_{S,0} OR h_{S,1}: at most d_{t+1} gates, and d_{t+1} <= 2d_t. Total = 2d_t + 2d_t + 2d_t = 6d_t. The claimed 4d_t bound is not justified by the given construction. A valid bound is 6d_t (or 7d_t as noted in S0815). The 4d_t claim is incorrect.

Mathematical verification of the constructive upper bound: (1) For each of the 2^r witness strings w∈{0,1}^r, substitute the fixed prefix p and the fixed witness w into the h-gate circuit H. This yields a circuit on the remaining variables z with at most h gates (substitution of constants and fixed inputs does not increase gate count). (2) Compute the OR of these 2^r outputs using a binary tree of 2^r - 1 two-input OR gates. (3) The resulting circuit outputs 1 iff at least one witness makes H(pz,w)=1, which is exactly E_p(z). (4) Gate count: 2^r * h (for the cofactored subcircuits) + (2^r - 1) (for the OR tree) = 2^r h + 2^r - 1. (5) Edge case r=0: 2^0=1 witness (empty string), 0 OR gates, total = h gates, which matches the formula. The bound is a valid constructive upper bound for the projected residual; it does not claim minimality or polynomial dependence on r. No counterexample exists for this constructive claim.

Verified the construction and gate count. For each destination S in R_{t+1} and bit b, E_{S,b} = {R in R_t : R_b = S}. The one-hot source bits e_R feed OR trees g_{S,b} = OR_{R in E_{S,b}} e_R (empty group -> constant 0). Sum of |E_{S,b}| over all (S,b) equals 2d_t (each source has exactly two children). Number of nonempty groups <= 2d_t. OR gates: sum_{nonempty} (|E|-1) = 2d_t - (#nonempty) <= 2d_t - 1. AND gates: h_{S,b} = g_{S,b} AND (b=b) uses one AND per nonempty group (<= 2d_t) and one shared NOT for NOT b. Final outputs: y_S = h_{S,0} OR h_{S,1} uses d_{t+1} <= 2d_t OR gates. Total gates <= (2d_t - 1) + 2d_t + 1 + 2d_t = 6d_t <= 7d_t for d_t >= 1. On valid one-hot input (exactly one e_R=1), exactly the coordinate for R_b becomes 1. The construction is level-specific, uses fan-in-two AND/OR and unary NOT, constants/wires free. No gap found. The bound is correct as stated.

Verified the construction and gate counts. For each of the 2^r witnesses w, the state bit q_w is updated as q'_w = q_w AND (x_i == H_i(w)). Since H_i(w) is a constant for fixed w, the transition uses at most h gates to evaluate H_i(w) (which can be hardwired as a constant 0 or 1, making this even smaller) plus 1 AND gate per w. With 2^r witnesses, transition cost <= 2^r(h+1). Acceptance is OR of all q_w, using 2^r - 1 OR gates. The bounds O(2^r(h+1)) for transition and O(2^r) for acceptance are correct. The lemma explicitly disclaims any lower bound or relation to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits. No gap found.

proved_step: RESIDUAL-STATE CHARACTERIZATION FOR FIXED-LENGTH STREAMING. Let L⊆{0,1}^N. For each t and p∈{0,1}^t, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}: pz∈L}. In any deterministic streaming recognizer of L, two length-t prefixes can lead to the same state only if their residuals are equal; conversely, a recognizer with one state for each distinct residual at each depth recognizes L. Proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. Equal states after p and q would force identical acceptance on the common continuation z, contradicting that exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. For the converse, transition the state R_p on bit b to R_{pb}={u:bu∈R_p}; at depth N accept iff the residual contains the empty string. Induction on the number of read bits shows the state after p is exactly R_p, so the machine recognizes L. This is a state characterization and gives no gate-cost bound for implementing transitions from H_C.

statement: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX-PROJECTION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let C_1,...,C_M be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on N input bits, each with at most g fan-in-two gates. For a prefix p of length t define E(p)=1 iff there exist i in [M] and z in {0,1}^{N-t} such that C_i(pz)=1. Then E has a fan-in-two circuit with at most M 2^{N-t}(g+1)-1 gates, assuming constants and wiring are free. Any further fixed prefix cofactor satisfies the same bound with the shortened suffix length.
derivation: For every pair (i,z) in [M] x {0,1}^{N-t}, create a copy of C_i, hardwire p and z, and take the OR of all M 2^{N-t} outputs using a binary fan-in-two tree. This uses at most M 2^{N-t}g + (M 2^{N-t}-1) gates. Further hardwiring inputs cannot increase gate count.
scope: All finite N,M,g and prefixes p; explicit finite circuit family. No polynomial bound is asserted when M or 2^{N-t} grows.

statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY OR AND COFACTOR BOUND. Let C_1,...,C_M be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on the same N input bits, each with at most g fan-in-two gates. The function F(x)=OR_{i=1}^M C_i(x) has a fan-in-two circuit with at most Mg+M-1 gates. For every fixed prefix p, the cofactor F_p has a circuit with at most the same number of gates.
derivation: Take disjoint copies of the M circuits and combine their outputs with a fan-in-two OR tree, which has M-1 gates. This computes F using at most Mg+M-1 gates. Substituting constants for any fixed prefix inputs in this circuit cannot increase its number of gates, so the cofactor has the same upper bound.
scope: All finite M>=1,N,g>=0, explicitly listed Boolean circuits, fan-in-two gates, constants and wiring free. This does not cover an implicitly represented family without an explicit listing or a bound on the cost of generating the family.

gap: The explicit-family OR/cofactor bound does not represent the implicit family of all size-<=s circuits defining EXT, nor does it bound the real-gate cost of transitions for an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C. The unresolved task is to identify what information an EXT algorithm needs and whether its transitions admit a bounded-operation representation using H_C, with cost measured in real gates rather than oracle calls.

proved_step:
statement: PREFIX LANGUAGE PARENT-CHILD RECURRENCE. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t<=N define E_L(p)=1 exactly when some string x in L extends p. If t<N, then E_L(p)=E_L(p0) OR E_L(p1). Consequently, if a circuit computes E_L on all prefixes at level t+1 (with p fixed and one suffix bit as input), the value at p is obtained by one OR gate from the two child acceptance bits; this recurrence alone does not compute either child predicate.
derivation: The completions of p are the disjoint union of strings extending p0 and strings extending p1. Thus at least one member of L extends p iff at least one of p0,p1 has an extension in L. The Boolean OR of the two indicator bits is exactly E_L(p).
scope: Every finite N, every language L subset {0,1}^N, every prefix p of length t<N. No circuit-size bound on computing E_L's child values is asserted.

gap: G0205 remains open. The parent value of an exact prefix language is the OR of its two child values, but this does not provide either child value from an arbitrary decision circuit H_C for MCSP, nor bound the real-gate cost of a transition that computes EXT membership on a prefix.

proved_step:
statement: SURVIVING-DESCRIPTION DERIVATIVE LEMMA. Let D be a finite set of descriptions, each denoting a string f_d in {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t<N, define S(p)={d in D: f_d has prefix p}. For b in {0,1}, S(pb)={d in S(p): the (t+1)-st bit of f_d is b}. The residual language after p is exactly {suffix_t(f_d): d in S(p)}. Proof: By definition, d survives p iff its first t bits equal p. It survives pb iff its first t bits equal p and its next bit equals b, which is equivalent to d in S(p) with next bit b. A string q of length N-t is in the residual language after p iff pq=f_d for some d in D, equivalent to d surviving p and q being the remaining suffix. Thus filtering survivors computes the next semantic state, and projecting survivors gives the exact residual language. This does not bound the cost of representing S(p), grouping duplicate suffixes, or finding S(p) for circuit descriptions.
scope: All finite D and N, and every map d -> f_d in {0,1}^N. Semantic identity only; no succinct encoding or transition-cost bound.
derivation: Unpack prefix membership and concatenate p with a suffix q.
evidence: DISCOVERY run cm-71bbbc3708024dee checked 24 derivative cases and 17 residual classes for the four-string family in its code. The general result follows from the direct set-membership proof, not the finite run.

statement: FINITE-CANDIDATE TRIE STATE BOUND FOR EXT. Let D be a finite family of M binary words of common length N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pu is in D}. The prefix automaton with one state for each distinct nonempty residual R(p), plus a rejecting sink, recognizes D and has at most MN+2 states. Its transition on b from R(p) is R(pb)={u:bu is in R(p)}. It accepts at depth N precisely when R(p) is nonempty. Therefore its states admit an encoding of ceil(log2(MN+2)) bits. If D is generated by descriptions of length at most L, then the number of descriptions is less than 2^(L+1), so the encoding requires O(L+log N) bits. Proof: Each of the M words contributes at most N nonempty prefixes, hence at most MN nonempty trie nodes; include the root if needed and one rejecting sink. Merging nodes with equal residual languages does not increase the count. For any suffix u, u is in R(pb) exactly when pbu is in D, which holds exactly when bu is in R(p); this proves the transition identity. At depth N, the only suffix is empty, so residual nonemptiness is equivalent to p belonging to D. An injective index encoding uses ceil(log2 K) bits for K states. Counting descriptions gives M<2^(L+1), and thus log2(MN+2)=O(L+log N). This proves state size and exact transition semantics only; it gives no gate-cost bound for computing transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
derivation: Count prefixes in the trie, derive the child residual by concatenation, and encode the finite state set by an index. The circuit corollary counts descriptions, not distinct outputs.
scope: Every finite D subset of {0,1}^N, N>=1. The description corollary assumes an explicit binary encoding with at most 2^(L+1) descriptions of length at most L. No transition computation cost is asserted.

statement: EXT CANDIDATE FILTERING IDENTITY. Fix n,s and a finite set C_{n,s} of descriptions of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with each description c computing f_c:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, N=2^n, the truth-table word in a fixed input order. For a prefix p of length t define A(p)={c in C_{n,s}: the first t bits of f_c equal p}. Then A(pb)={c in A(p): the (t+1)-st bit of f_c equals b}. The EXT residual language R(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: exists c in C_{n,s}, f_c=p||u} equals {suffix_t(f_c):c in A(p)}. Consequently EXT prefix state can be represented exactly by the surviving circuit descriptions A(p), and the next-bit update is a filter on their next output bit. Proof: By definition, c belongs to A(pb) iff its first t+1 output bits are p||b, which is equivalent to its first t bits being p and its next bit being b; this proves the filter identity. A suffix u belongs to R(p) iff there exists c with f_c=p||u, equivalently c belongs to A(p) and its remaining suffix is u; this proves the residual identity. The argument is finite and exact. It gives neither a succinct representation of A(p) beyond listing descriptions nor a bound on the real-gate cost of filtering it, and therefore does not imply a transition-cost reduction for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Expand the definitions of the image prefix residual and the surviving-description set; split equality of output prefixes at the (t+1)th bit.
scope: Any finite circuit-description set C_{n,s}, fixed output truth-table order, and all prefixes of lengths 0 through N. No uniformity or efficient-update bound asserted.

statement: EXPLICIT ENUMERATION UPDATE BOUND FOR EXT. Fix n,s and let D be the set of all syntactically valid fan-in-two Boolean circuit descriptions on n inputs with at most s gates, under a fixed encoding of length O(s log(n+s)). Let M=|D|, and list D in a fixed order. For each prefix p of length t of the truth table, store the M-bit vector v_t whose d-th bit is 1 exactly when circuit d agrees with p on its first t truth-table positions, together with the t counter. On reading the next bit b, evaluate each circuit d on the input assignment indexed by t; set its next membership bit to v_t[d] AND [f_d(t)=b], then increment t. This update is exact: by induction on t, v_t[d]=1 iff d agrees with p on the first t positions, so v_{t+1} represents exactly the circuits agreeing with pb. The state uses M+n bits. If evaluating one listed circuit on one input takes O(s) time, a direct sequential update takes O(Ms+n) time per input bit. The description count satisfies M <= 2^{O(s log(n+s))}, so this gives an explicit, generally exponential-resource transition procedure. It does not imply a polynomial transition bound for compressed encodings or a lower bound for arbitrary representations.
derivation: Initialize every membership bit to 1 at t=0. At step t, each candidate's next truth-table bit is obtained by evaluating its circuit on the t-th assignment. Filtering by equality to b preserves exactly those candidates consistent with the extended prefix. Induction proves the invariant for every t. The memory and time bounds follow from storing M bits and evaluating M circuits, each with at most s gates.
scope: All finite n,s and the stated circuit encoding; sequential evaluation time assumes circuit descriptions are explicitly available and each gate evaluation costs O(1).

statement: EXPLICIT ENUMERATION UPDATE PROCEDURE FOR EXT. Fix n,s and a fixed, explicitly enumerable list D of M fan-in-two Boolean circuit descriptions on n inputs, each with at most s gates. For a truth-table prefix p of length t, store the M-bit vector v_t with v_t[d]=1 iff circuit d agrees with p on positions 0 through t-1, and an n-bit counter for t (the case t=2^n is handled by a separate terminal flag). On reading bit b, generate the n-bit input assignment x_t indexed by t, then for each d set v_{t+1}[d]=v_t[d] AND [f_d(x_t)=b], and advance the counter. For every t, the invariant v_t[d]=1 iff d agrees with p on its first t positions follows by induction: it holds initially because the empty prefix imposes no constraint, and the update retains exactly candidates whose next output equals b. Thus the update is exact and the prefix is extendible within the represented family iff some bit of v_t is 1. If generating x_t takes O(n) time and evaluating one listed circuit on x_t takes O(s) time, the update takes O(n+Ms) time and the mutable state uses M+n+O(1) bits; the fixed description list is read-only program data. Since a standard gate-list encoding has M <= 2^{O(s log(n+s))}, this is generally exponential in s and n. This procedure gives no lower bound for compressed or arbitrary representations, so it does not close G0004.
derivation: Use the stated candidate-membership invariant. At position t, compute the corresponding assignment once, evaluate each still-live circuit, and filter by equality with the arriving bit. The induction proves exactness. The stated time sums one O(n) assignment-generation cost and M evaluations of O(s) each; the stored membership vector and counter give the state bound.
scope: All finite n,s and any fixed explicit circuit list D under the stated costs. The universal update-computation lower bound for all representations remains open.

gap: G0004 remains open: determine whether an update-computation lower bound for exact Search-MCSP^A transitions holds for every representation with polynomial workspace, including nonlinear/time-dependent encodings, redundant states, shared intermediate computation, arbitrary fan-out, deferred work, and alternative witnesses. The explicit candidate-filtering procedure is only an upper bound for one representation.

statement: SURVIVOR-BITSET TRANSITION FOR EXT. Fix n and a finite family D of Boolean circuits on n input bits, with |D|=M, and fix an ordering x_1,...,x_{2^n} of the truth-table inputs. For each prefix p of length t, let B_p be the M-bit vector whose d-coordinate is 1 exactly when circuit d's truth table begins with p. Given t, B_p, and the next bit b, B_{pb} is computed coordinatewise by (B_{pb})_d=(B_p)_d AND [d(x_{t+1})=b]. Thus the transition has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most 2M gates when the constants [d(x_{t+1})=b] are supplied for this fixed t,b; decoder acceptance is OR of the M coordinates. For EXT_{n,s}, take D to contain one representative for each n-input circuit of size at most s. This gives an exact, explicit transition procedure with M=|D| state bits and O(M) transition gates per fixed position. Proof: d survives prefix p exactly when its first t truth-table bits equal p. It survives the child prefix pb exactly when it survives p and its next truth-table bit equals b. The displayed coordinate formula is precisely this equivalence, independently for each d. OR of the coordinates is 1 exactly when some circuit in D extends p. No claim is made that this representation is minimal or polynomial in s.
derivation: Enumerate the finite circuit family D. Store one survivor bit per description. For each coordinate, update by AND with the fixed indicator that the circuit's next output bit equals b. By induction on prefix length, the stored coordinates are exactly the descriptions extending the current prefix. The decoder OR therefore recognizes EXT. Each coordinate uses at most one AND gate; a binary OR tree uses at most M−1 gates.
scope: All finite n, s, fixed circuit families D, and fixed truth-table input order. The transition circuit is position-specific (t is fixed in its constants); no bound polynomial in s is asserted. The state width M may be exponential in s log(n+s), and this does not establish a transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

evidence: Direct set-theoretic proof, including empty and full-prefix cases.

statement: SURVIVOR SET IS A SUFFICIENT STATE FOR EXT. Fix n, a finite family D of Boolean circuits on n input bits, and an ordering x_1,...,x_{2^n} of the inputs. For a prefix p of length t, define S_p={d in D: d(x_i)=p_i for every 1<=i<=t}. Then (i) p is an extendible truth-table prefix iff S_p is nonempty; and (ii) for any next bit b, S_{pb}={d in S_p: d(x_{t+1})=b}. Proof: If p is extendible, by definition some d in D agrees with p at every listed position, so d lies in S_p; conversely any d in S_p supplies a completion, namely its remaining truth-table bits. For the transition identity, d belongs to S_{pb} exactly when it agrees with p on the first t positions and has value b at x_{t+1}, which is precisely membership in the displayed filtered set. Hence the survivor set, with nonemptiness as decoder, is an exact sufficient state for every prefix transition.
derivation: Both assertions follow by expanding the definition of S_p coordinatewise. Membership is exactly agreement with the prefix; appending b adds exactly one agreement condition.
scope: All finite n, all finite families D of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n (in particular circuit families), all input orders, all prefixes including t=0 and t=2^n. This is a sufficient-state lemma only; it gives no compact encoding or low-cost transition from H_C.

statement: FINITE CANDIDATE-AGREEMENT AUTOMATON WITH EXPLICIT UPDATE COST. Let N be a nonnegative integer and F=(f_1,...,f_M) an ordered finite family of strings in {0,1}^N, allowing M=0 and repetitions. For each t in {0,...,N}, each prefix p in {0,1}^t, and each i, define q_t(i)=1 iff the first t bits of f_i equal p. The vector q_t is an exact state for the surviving candidates; p has an extension in F iff OR_i q_t(i)=1. Given p's next bit b at position t+1, the transition is q_{t+1}(i)=q_t(i) AND [f_i(t+1)=b] for every i. With F and the position-dependent constants fixed in the transition, this is implemented by at most M fan-in-two AND gates. Proof: At t=0 the empty prefix agrees with every f_i, so the stated invariant holds. Assume it holds at t. A candidate f_i agrees with the length-(t+1) prefix pb exactly when it agrees with p and its (t+1)-st bit equals b. This equivalence is precisely the displayed update, so induction proves the invariant for all t. The prefix has an extension in F exactly when at least one candidate agrees with it, which is equivalent to OR_i q_t(i)=1; for M=0 this OR is the constant 0. Each coordinate update is either q_t(i) AND 1, or q_t(i) AND 0, according to the fixed candidate bit and b; one AND gate per coordinate suffices (and constants may simplify it). This proves the transition bound. The result gives no compression of the M-bit state, no useful bound on M in terms of circuit size parameters, and no representation or transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
derivation: Induction on prefix length using the exact equivalence: candidate i matches pb iff it matches p and its next bit is b. The extendibility output is the OR of the agreement coordinates. Implement each coordinate by one AND with the appropriate fixed comparison bit.
scope: Every finite N, every ordered finite family F subset {0,1}^N including the empty family and repeated strings, and every prefix length 0<=t<=N; explicit M-coordinate representation only.

statement: RIGHT-RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION OF EXACT PREFIX STATES. Let L be any finite binary language and, for each prefix p, define R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz is a prefix of some word in L}. In any deterministic prefix-processing automaton that exactly tracks whether the current prefix can be extended to a word in L, two prefixes assigned the same state must have equal right residuals R_p. Conversely, equality R_p=R_q permits identifying p and q while preserving all future extendibility answers. Thus the minimal exact state partition is equality of right residuals; the number of required states is the number of distinct sets R_p.
derivation: For necessity, if z belongs to exactly one of R_p and R_q, then after reading z the exact extendibility answer differs, whereas a deterministic automaton starting from the same state and reading the same z must reach the same state and answer identically, a contradiction. For sufficiency, if R_p=R_q, then for every continuation z the extendibility answers agree by definition, so merging p and q preserves every future answer. Equality of residuals is therefore both necessary and sufficient for state equivalence, and the quotient by that equivalence is the minimal exact partition.
scope: Every finite binary language L, including the finite language Im(Eval_{n,s}) defining EXT_{n,s}. This characterizes state information only; it gives no bound on transition time or on real-gate operations over H_C.

gap: The assigned EXT-versus-H_C connection still lacks a bound on the real-gate cost of implementing an EXT residual transition from H_C, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits has been established.
